source_issues.title: [Bug] stream_events=True prevents TeamRunPausedEvent from being emitted (HITL broken)
source_issues.evidence: When using stream_events=True with team.arun(), TeamRunPausedEvent is never emitted even when a member agent's tool has requires_confirmation=True. Without stream_events=True, the same code works correctly. stream_events=True is needed for real-time UI updates (tool call progress, plan tracking). Without it, applications cannot show live progress during team execution while supporting HITL.

signals.topic: MCP tool wrapper silently drops structuredContent breaking MCP Apps generative UI
signals.summary: MCPTools discards the structuredContent field of MCP CallToolResult when converting to ToolResult. Since the rendered UI JSON tree for MCP Apps lives in structuredContent, downstream clients (CopilotKit, AG-UI hosts) cannot render the UI and must re-invoke the tool as a wasteful workaround.
signals.review_reason: This breaks a key feature: MCP Apps generative UI rendering. structuredContent (the canonical channel for machine-readable tool output including rendered UI trees) is silently dropped. MCP Apps clients cannot render UI without re-invoking the tool, a wasteful workaround. This is significant feature unavailability for MCP Apps users. Count=1 single repo defaults to P1.

source_issues.title: [Bug] MCP: `CallToolResult.structuredContent` is silently dropped by the tool wrapper
source_issues.evidence: MCPTools discards structuredContent field of MCP CallToolResult when converting to ToolResult. For MCP Apps, the rendered UI JSON tree lives in structuredContent and is dropped, meaning clients (CopilotKit, AG-UI hosts) cannot render the UI without a separate redundant tool call. This breaks a key feature (MCP Apps generative UI) and requires a wasteful workaround of re-invoking the tool.

signals.topic: MCP tool wrapper silently drops CallToolResult._meta breaking observability and structured metadata
signals.summary: MCPTools discards the _meta field of MCP CallToolResult when converting to ToolResult. Since _meta is the MCP protocol's out-of-band channel for trace IDs, rate-limit hints, pagination cursors, and application-specific payloads, its silent drop breaks observability, debugging, and any structured contract between MCP servers and clients.
signals.review_reason: This breaks observability and structured metadata access for all MCP tool results. _meta is the MCP protocol's out-of-band channel for trace ids, rate-limit hints, pagination cursors, and application-specific payloads. Its silent drop means Agno users cannot access critical metadata that MCP servers intentionally attach. This is significant UX degradation for any MCP integration relying on metadata. Count=1 single repo defaults to P1.

source_issues.title: [Bug] MCP: `CallToolResult._meta` is silently dropped by the tool wrapper
source_issues.evidence: MCPTools discards the _meta field of MCP CallToolResult when converting to ToolResult. _meta is the out-of-band channel for structured metadata (trace ids, provenance, confidence scores, rate-limit hints). Dropping this breaks observability, debugging, and any structured contract between MCP servers and clients. Every MCP server using _meta is unreachable via Agno even though the underlying mcp SDK preserves the field correctly.

signals.topic: Code output gets silently truncated after 1-2 words when agent writes code
signals.summary: When OpenCode's agent writes code, the output is silently cut off after 1-2 words, making code generation completely unusable. Multiple users confirmed the same issue across different models, skills, and agents — core coding workflow is blocked.
signals.review_reason: Code generation is the primary use case of OpenCode. Silent truncation of code output blocks the core coding workflow entirely. Multiple users confirmed the same behavior across different models and agents, indicating a systemic issue. The fact that it affects all models equally points to a client-side parsing or streaming bug rather than a model-specific problem.

source_issues.title: Code gets cutoff, no matter what
source_issues.evidence: User reports code output stops after 1-2 words when agent writes code. Confirmed across multiple models (independent of model, skills, or agent). Multiple Discord users experienced the same issue per author. Full session log attached showing cutoff pattern.

signals.topic: Audio oscillator leak after logo mouseout — coreaudiod CPU pinned at 480%, painful continuous noise on headphones
signals.summary: The TUI logo charge/burst audio feature leaves oscillator nodes running after mouseout. On macOS, coreaudiod pins a CPU core at 480%+ (M4 Max). The generated tone degrades into continuous loud scratching/buzzing on the audio output device, requiring users to physically kill OpenCode or yank audio cables to stop it.
signals.review_reason: This bug causes a runaway oscillator that consumes 480%+ CPU on a dedicated core and produces physically painful sustained noise through headphones — a real risk of hearing discomfort. It is not cosmetic: users have no in-app way to stop the audio, and the only workarounds are killing the process or physically disconnecting audio hardware. The issue is reproducible and the root cause (oscillator not torn down on mouseleave) is clearly identified.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Logo charge-hum audio leaks after mouseout: coreaudiod pinned at 480% CPU, painful continuous noise on output device
source_issues.evidence: Detailed bug report with M4 Max hardware specs. coreaudiod measured at 480.5% CPU. Author describes noise as 'physically painful' through headphones. No in-app way to stop audio — only mitigation is killing the process or power-cycling the audio device. Related issue #22528 also requests audio toggle and remains open. Root cause traced to PR #22098 oscillator/gain lifecycle bug.

signals.topic: SIGTERM/SIGINT leaves OpenCode hanging — MCP servers, LSP clients, PTYs, and file watchers orphaned
signals.summary: When OpenCode receives SIGTERM or SIGINT (e.g., `killall opencode`), the TUI window closes but the process hangs. Bun Worker, Effect runtimes, MCP servers, LSP clients, PTYs, and file watchers are all orphaned. Only SIGHUP triggers graceful teardown; SIGTERM and SIGINT bypass the terminal event handler entirely.
signals.review_reason: SIGTERM/SIGINT are standard OS-level termination signals — when `killall opencode` leaves the process hanging and orphans MCP servers, LSP clients, PTYs, and file watchers, this directly impacts developer workflow. Resources are leaked, and users must manually find and kill orphaned processes. The issue has precise root cause analysis and a locally verified fix.

source_issues.title: SIGTERM hangs, does not output anything
source_issues.evidence: Author provides precise root cause analysis: only SIGHUP is wired to the exit() teardown path. SIGTERM/SIGINT bypass terminal event handling entirely, leaving Bun Worker and all child processes (MCP servers, LSP clients, PTYs, file watchers) orphaned. Verified locally with fix available (adding signal handlers next to existing SIGHUP handler in exit.tsx:57). Reproduced on Debian Linux + tmux/ghostty/kitty.

signals.topic: Editor silently injects 'Note: The user opened the file' on every prompt — pollutes AI context for all sessions
signals.summary: When the editor has any file open with a cursor but no text selected, OpenCode silently injects 'Note: The user opened the file /path/to/file' into every AI prompt submission. The user never sees this message — only the AI does. It fires on every prompt as long as any file has focus, making every conversation polluted with irrelevant context that degrades response quality.
aliases: synthetic file note on every prompt
Note: user opened file injected silently
signals.review_reason: This silently pollutes every AI prompt with irrelevant context for all users who keep files open in their editor while using OpenCode. It degrades AI response quality across all conversations with no user-visible indication and no way to disable it. While not a hard block, it represents a persistent quality-of-experience regression for the majority of users who work with files open.

source_issues.title: Editor context injects 'Note: The user opened the file' on every prompt when cursor is in a file
source_issues.evidence: Author provides exact code location: Y.selection() returns a value whenever editor has focus, and start===end branch always resolves to 'Note: The user opened the file' on every prompt. This affects every conversation as long as any file is open in the editor. The synthetic note is invisible to the user but sent to the AI on every single message.

signals.topic: Desktop app: opening settings interrupts and terminates ongoing sessions
signals.summary: In the OpenCode desktop app (v1.14.28, macOS), opening the settings panel while a coding session is active immediately interrupts and terminates the session. The expected behavior is that the session continues in the background.
signals.review_reason: This bug causes an active coding session to be terminated when the user opens settings — a routine and expected interaction in a desktop app. Users cannot configure settings mid-session without losing their work, which is a significant UX failure for a desktop application where background session persistence is a basic expectation.

source_issues.title: Opening settings for Opencode desktop interrupts ongoing session
source_issues.evidence: User reports step-by-step reproduction: start a session, open settings, session is interrupted. Version 1.14.28 on macOS desktop. Expected behavior (session continues in background) is clearly defined. Reporter is specifically on the desktop app.

signals.topic: JSONOutputFormatParam.Type field elided from request body, causing API to silently hang structured-output requests
signals.summary: When using JSONOutputFormatParam without explicitly setting Type, the field is silently omitted from the marshaled JSON. The API hangs indefinitely instead of returning a 400, causing requests to time out after 10 minutes. This blocks structured output workflows entirely.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is completely blocked: structured-output requests silently hang until 10-minute timeout. The bug is reproducible and well-documented with a clear root cause (struct tag + marshaling behavior). Strong user impact evidence: same request works in Python SDK, fails in Go SDK, with packet-level confirmation of the missing field.

source_issues.title: JSONOutputFormatParam.Type elided from request body, causes API to hang structured-output requests
source_issues.evidence: The 'type' field is silently omitted from the marshaled request body. When the field is missing, the Anthropic API hangs indefinitely (no 400 response) and the request times out after 10 minutes via CalculateNonStreamingTimeout. Same prompt completes in seconds via Python SDK. Workaround requires a custom RoundTripper to inject the missing field.

signals.topic: invopop/jsonschema v0.14.0 type mismatch causes SDK compilation failure in consuming modules
signals.summary: The SDK declares invopop/jsonschema v0.13.0 in its go.mod but uses wk8/go-ordered-map internally. When a consuming module resolves invopop/jsonschema v0.14.0 (which switched to pb33f/ordered-map), the SDK fails to compile due to ordered-map type incompatibility in schemautil.go.
signals.review_reason: Build failure blocks SDK integration into consuming projects. This is a dependency version conflict that is non-trivial to work around (requires manually pinning transitive dependencies). While only count=1, the impact is significant: the SDK cannot be compiled in projects with newer jsonschema dependencies.

source_issues.title: Build failure: invopop/jsonschema v0.14.0 incompatibility (pb33f vs wk8 ordered-map type mismatch in schemautil.go)
source_issues.evidence: SDK fails to compile when consuming module has invopop/jsonschema v0.14.0 or later resolved. Error: type mismatch between wk8/go-ordered-map and pb33f/ordered-map in schemautil.go:99. Workaround requires pinning invopop/jsonschema to v0.13.0 in the consuming module's go.mod.

signals.topic: Embedded reflect.Type usage disables Go linker dead-code elimination, inflating binary sizes
signals.summary: The SDK internally embeds reflect.Type (likely via generated code), which causes Go's linker to include all SDK symbols even when unused. This prevents dead-code elimination and significantly increases binary size for consumers.
signals.review_reason: This is a build/linker optimization issue causing binary size inflation. While not a workflow-blocking failure, it causes tangible cost (larger binaries, slower deploys) and is a well-known pattern issue in generated Go SDKs. Referenced cross-SDK issue confirms the pattern is recognized.

source_issues.title: bug: embedded reflect.Type breaks Go linker dead-code elimination
source_issues.evidence: SDK usage disables dead-code elimination in consuming projects. Referenced upstream issue openai/openai-go#609. This is a known pattern in auto-generated SDKs using reflection-based encoding.

signals.topic: Java quickstart documentation is broken (missing classpath setup, outdated Maven version)
signals.summary: The Java SDK quickstart page instructs users to run `javac QuickStart.java` and `java QuickStart` without any classpath configuration, causing immediate compilation failure. Additionally, the Maven/Gradle snippets reference version `2.20.0` which does not exist on Maven Central (latest is `2.26.0`), returning 404 errors. Users following the official quickstart cannot run the SDK at all.
aliases: javac java classpath missing in docs
signals.review_reason: 该问题造成主流程阻断：新用户按照官方快速开始文档无法编译运行任何 Java SDK 代码，因为 (1) javac/java 缺少 classpath 配置导致编译失败；(2) Maven/Gradle 引用的版本号在 Maven Central 上不存在。属于文档层面的阻断性缺陷，直接影响新用户体验和 SDK 采用。count=1 为该主题唯一 issue，虽不满足高频条件，但明确的主流程失败证据支撑保留为 P1。

source_issues.title: Java quickstart docs: javac/java commands don't work without classpath setup, version 2.20.0 doesn't exist
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告按照官方快速开始文档执行 `javac`/`java` 命令立即失败，因为没有配置 classpath；Maven/Gradle 引用的版本 2.20.0 在 Maven Central 上不存在，访问返回 404。用户完全无法运行 SDK。

signals.topic: Back-to-back prompt cache writes: identical cache prefix billed repeatedly (~40% miss rate, resolved by 2s sleep)
signals.summary: When two sequential API calls share an identical cached system prompt, the second call misses the cache ~40% of the time and re-writes the same prefix, causing direct cost duplication. Sleeping 2s between calls reliably eliminates the miss, indicating an API-side cache-visibility race condition.
signals.review_reason: 用户直接资金损失：相同前缀的缓存被重复计费，在典型 agent 负载（10-100K tokens/请求）下，多轮对话的每一个第二轮请求都有~40%概率全额重复付费。Issue提供了完整的可复现脚本和明确的数据（8/20失败率），确认是API侧缓存可见性竞态而非SDK问题。

source_issues.title: Cache misses on second back-to-back `client.messages.create()` (~40% rate)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced 8/20 back-to-back calls re-wrote identical cache prefix at full cache_creation_input_tokens rate. Sleep 2s eliminates all misses. Direct cost impact: same tokens billed twice. Referenced related issue anthropics/claude-code#38356 (closed unresolved) with matching symptoms.

signals.topic: Streaming stalls 50–180s at large tool-call argument boundary (~100K input tokens, Sonnet 4.6)
signals.summary: When streaming requests with ~100K+ input tokens invoke a tool requiring a large argument payload (e.g. 25K tokens of generated code), the SSE stream goes completely silent for 50–180 seconds at the transition to the arguments field, before the first argument token arrives. Reproduced via direct curl, ruling out SDK-level issues.
aliases: SSE stream hangs on large tool arguments
streaming timeout on high-token tool calls
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：流式响应在工具调用参数边界处完全静默50-180秒，极易触发客户端超时阈值，导致整个请求失败。这是使用流式API的核心使用场景受阻，且已通过直接curl复现排除客户端SDK问题。

source_issues.title: Stream stalls for 50–180s before next token when generating large tool call arguments (~100K input tokens)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced via direct API call (curl) with chunk-level timing logs: stream stalls for 75+ seconds at exact argument-field transition point. Affects both Bedrock-hosted and direct API models. User has ~108-118 tools in request. Same workload completes without stalling on GPT-5.4.

signals.topic: ToolUseBlock caller field type mismatch: 400 BadRequest on Bedrock when converting response to request param
signals.summary: ToolUseBlock has caller: Optional[Caller] = None but ToolUseBlockParam requires caller: Caller (non-nullable). When .to_dict() is called (or via transform pipeline), the None value triggers a 400 BadRequestError on Bedrock client after tool execution, breaking the roundtrip pattern.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：Bedrock用户在使用工具后无法将结果发回API，所有工具调用后第二轮请求均返回400错误。虽存在变通方案（exclude_none=True），但用户必须知晓SDK内部行为才能规避，影响真实生产使用。

source_issues.title: ToolUseBlock and ToolUseBlockParam type conflict for caller nullability
source_issues.evidence: Bedrock client throws 'Error code: 400 - messages.13.content.1.tool_use.caller: Input should be a valid dictionary' after sending tool result back. Does not occur with vertex/anthropic clients. Workaround: explicit .to_dict(exclude_none=True). Root cause: Bedrock sets 'caller' field in response, which is None in ToolUseBlock and fails ToolUseBlockParam validation.

signals.topic: BetaCitationPageLocation file_id=null breaks multi-turn roundtrip: BadRequestError on follow-up request
signals.summary: When a document is provided via URL (not file_id), the API returns BetaCitationPageLocation with file_id: null. The corresponding request param type BetaCitationPageLocationParam has no file_id field. Using model_dump(mode='json') to echo the response into the next request passes file_id: null to the API, which rejects it with BadRequestError, breaking the standard multi-turn conversation pattern.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：BetaCitationPageLocation在使用URL文档时含file_id=null，该字段无法通过API请求参数校验，导致所有含引用（citations）的多轮对话在第二轮全部失败。用户必须手动编写清理函数，这是SDK核心设计缺陷（响应类型和请求类型不对称）。

source_issues.title: `BetaCitationPageLocation` contains `file_id` that cannot be roundtripped as a request
source_issues.evidence: Verified via _transform_typeddict: file_id: None survives the transform pipeline because the field is unknown to BetaCitationPageLocationParam, falling through to the 'unknown field' branch. Causes BadRequestError when echoing citation-bearing assistant messages in follow-up requests. No automatic fix in SDK. Requires manual sanitization function.

signals.topic: Intermittent 404 NotFoundError crashes Batch API: server-side propagation delay across infrastructure nodes
signals.summary: After successfully creating a message batch, subsequent calls to batches.retrieve() and batches.results() intermittently return 404 Not Found due to transient server-side propagation delay across Anthropic infrastructure nodes. In the worst case, batches.results() (called after status was confirmed 'ended') also returns 404, crashing the application because results() internally calls retrieve().
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：batches.results()在状态确认为ended后仍返回404导致应用崩溃，batches.create()本身也可能返回404导致批处理完全无法启动。这是批量处理核心功能在生产环境中被间歇性阻断，且无可靠SDK层防护。

source_issues.title: Intermittent `NotFoundError (404)` on Batch API
source_issues.evidence: Three distinct failure cases within 15-minute window: (1) retrieve() returns 404 1s after successful create(), (2) results() crashes with 404 after status was 'ended', (3) create() itself returns 404. Full traceback provided. All three request_ids share prefix req_011CaH... suggesting infrastructure-level issue. No SDK-level workaround available — application must catch and fall back.

signals.topic: Vertex SDK countTokens forwards anthropic-beta headers to models that reject them, causing HTTP 400 on lagging backends (e.g. Haiku)
signals.summary: When using Vertex AI backend, countTokens and its fallback path forward beta headers to underlying models. Vertex backends roll out new beta values on different schedules, causing HTTP 400 rejections on models (especially Haiku) that haven't received the latest beta. This causes recurring breakage in downstream consumers including Claude Code.
aliases: Haiku model HTTP 400 on beta headers
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure: countTokens with Vertex backend returns HTTP 400 on affected models, blocking token counting. Recurring pattern — every new beta introduction re-triggers the same failure. Downstream Claude Code is explicitly affected with a linked open issue. User impact is clear and repeated, not a one-off edge case.

source_issues.title: [Vertex] anthropic-beta header forwarded to countTokens fallback fails on lagging model backends
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 400 on Haiku models with beta headers; recurring breakage affecting Claude Code (open since Nov 2025); multiple beta values have caused the same failure (structured-outputs, tool-search, context-1m, redact-thinking, web-search)

signals.topic: Streaming with forced tool_choice: tool_use input arrives double-wrapped as { input: {...} } instead of raw arguments, breaking schema validation
signals.summary: When calling messages.stream with tool_choice forced to a specific tool, the tool_use block's input field is consistently wrapped one level deeper than the SDK type claims — { input: { actual args } } instead of { actual args }. This breaks Zod/schema validation since consumers validate against the tool's own input_schema.
signals.review_reason: Data inconsistency bug: the SDK type promises raw tool arguments but the actual streaming response delivers a double-wrapped envelope. This breaks schema validation (Zod safeParse fails on required fields) on every invocation with forced tool_choice, which is a common production pattern. Not intermittent — user reports it fires 100% of runs.

source_issues.title: tool_use block: toolUse.input arrives wrapped in an extra { input: {...} } envelope (streaming, forced tool_choice)
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible in production; breaks Zod schema validation for every top-level required field; workaround defensive unwrap fires on every run; observed across SDK versions 0.75.0 to 0.91.0; type ToolUseBlock.input claims raw args but actual payload is wrapped

signals.topic: betaZodTool return type BetaRunnableTool<T> is not assignable to ToolUnion required by messages.stream/messages.create, defeating type safety
signals.summary: The Ring 5 documentation recommends betaZodTool as the idiomatic way to define tools with Zod schemas, but its return type BetaRunnableTool<T> is not assignable to ToolUnion. This causes TS2322 at compile time, and the only workaround is an unsafe 'as unknown as' cast that throws away all the type safety betaZodTool was supposed to provide.
signals.review_reason: Type safety breakage: betaZodTool (the officially documented tool definition approach) is incompatible with the standard messages API at the type level. Developers following the docs hit a TS2322 and the only workaround is a cast that defeats the entire purpose of using Zod for type safety. This is a core DX regression for any TypeScript user adopting Ring 5 patterns.

source_issues.title: TS2322: Type BetaRunnableTool<{}> is not assignable to type ToolUnion
source_issues.evidence: TypeScript compilation error blocks use of betaZodTool with the standard messages API; workaround requires unsafe cast destroying type safety; Ring 5 docs present betaZodTool as the recommended approach but don't warn about incompatibility with messages.stream

signals.topic: Managed Agents API applies automatic prompt caching with no opt-out, causing unexpected 1.25x cache_creation_input_tokens charges
signals.summary: The Managed Agents Sessions API automatically applies prompt caching server-side with no client-side option to disable it. Unlike the Messages API where cache_control is opt-in, Managed Agents forces caching, resulting in cache_creation_input_tokens charges that users cannot avoid. For short-lived sessions or non-repeating prompts, this increases cost with no benefit.
aliases: Managed Agents forced caching no disable
unexpected prompt caching cost Managed Agents
signals.review_reason: Cost impact: automatic caching with no opt-out means users pay 1.25x on every Managed Agents session regardless of whether they benefit from caching. This is a clear financial harm for users with short-lived or non-repeating session patterns. Unlike the Messages API which exposes cache_control as opt-in, Managed Agents forces this cost.

source_issues.title: feat: Add option to disable automatic prompt caching in Managed Agents API
source_issues.evidence: Cache write tokens cost 1.25x standard input tokens; SessionCreateParams has no caching-related parameters; unlike Messages API (cache_control opt-in), Managed Agents applies caching automatically; user cannot opt out

signals.topic: SDK silently drops SSE ping events, preventing ping-aware watchdog; causes false-positive stream timeouts and Claude Code hangs
signals.summary: The Anthropic SSE stream emits ping events every 15-30s as a liveness signal, but the TypeScript SDK silently drops them (if event == 'ping' continue). Downstream clients including Claude Code cannot distinguish 'server actively thinking' from 'stream silently stalled'. This causes false-positive watchdog aborts during long model thinking (Opus can go silent 60-120s) and real hangs are indistinguishable from normal operation.
signals.review_reason: Structural reliability gap: the SDK drops the only liveness signal the server provides, forcing every downstream consumer (including Claude Code with 40+ hang reports) to guess whether a slow stream is normal thinking or a genuine hang. This causes false-positive aborts and undetected real hangs — both harmful. The fix (forward pings as events) is architecturally straightforward and would end a recurring class of bugs.

source_issues.title: Proposal: Ping-aware streaming watchdog (fixes #749, #867, and downstream Claude Code hangs)
source_issues.evidence: SDK code explicitly drops pings: 'if (event == ping) continue'; references multiple open issues (#749, #867) and 40+ downstream Claude Code hang reports (#46987); Opus thinking can go silent 60-120s between text deltas; Claude Code CLI re-implements watchdog from scratch but can't get liveness info from SDK

signals.topic: Windows: long system_prompt causes misleading CLINotFoundError due to cmdline overflow, no SDK fallback to --system-prompt-file
signals.summary: On Windows, when system_prompt exceeds the 32,767-char CreateProcess limit, the SDK raises a misleading CLINotFoundError instead of falling back to --system-prompt-file. The SDK already has this pattern for --agents but not for --system-prompt.
aliases: system_prompt file fallback missing on Windows
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow failure on Windows: users with RAG/memory-injected system_prompt (the natural integration pattern) are completely blocked at first non-trivial query. The error message is actively misleading — it says 'CLI not found' when the CLI exists and works fine, causing users to waste significant time reinstalling/configuring a binary that isn't missing. The fix pattern already exists in the codebase for --agents but was never applied to --system-prompt. Severity is compounded by the misleading diagnostic.

source_issues.title: Windows: SDK should fall back to --system-prompt-file when cmdline overflows (follow-up to #501)
source_issues.evidence: Windows 11 + Python 3.14, system_prompt ~48,755 chars triggers FileNotFoundError/WinError 206, SDK misattributes as 'CLI not found at path'. CLI binary exists and works standalone. Non-trivial RAG or memory-injected prompts hit this on first query. 90-min investigation wasted chasing a false binary-missing error.

signals.topic: TaskNotificationMessage delivered prematurely while subagent is still executing tool calls, causing orchestrator cascade failures
signals.summary: When orchestrator dispatches parallel subagents via Task tool, TaskNotificationMessage arrives before the subagent has finished all tool calls. Orchestrator acts on false completion signal, dispatching downstream agents against files that don't exist yet, causing wasted compute and incorrect results.
aliases: subagent still running when notification fires
orchestrator cascade from false completion signal
signals.review_reason: This causes incorrect orchestrator behavior (wrong downstream agent dispatches based on false completion signals), not just a degraded experience. The orchestrator's event-driven pattern is fundamentally broken — it acts on a signal that hasn't actually occurred. File state is wrong when reviewers run. While count=1, the user impact is severe: wasted compute, incorrect results, and the orchestrator gets flooded with stale notifications. This is a core SDK orchestration feature broken in a non-deterministic way.

source_issues.title: [Bug] TaskNotificationMessage fires while subagent is still running (premature, not cross-turn leak)
source_issues.evidence: Orchestrator dispatches 5 parallel subagents, all 5 sent premature <task-notification> while still mid-execution (subagent R2 was at tool 13 of 39, 466s before finishing). Orchestrator immediately dispatched 5 reviewers against files that didn't exist. Total wasted: 8 min of re-dispatched researcher time, 5 reviewers failed, stale TASK_DONE flood 17 min later. $21.51 in broken run vs $22.33 in correct identical run — incorrect results, not just wasted cost. Non-deterministic: 1 of 2 identical runs triggered.

signals.topic: MCP servers launched by SDK not cleaned up on process exit, leaving orphaned browser processes
signals.summary: When the SDK launches MCP servers (e.g., chrome-devtools), it does not clean them up on exit. Any browser launched by the MCP server remains open after the SDK session ends, causing resource leaks.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug (labeled 'bug' by maintainers) with clear reproduction: any session using MCP servers that spawn UI processes (e.g., browsers) leaves those processes orphaned. This is a resource leak — not a main-flow blocker, but violates user expectations that SDK-managed processes are SDK-managed lifecycle. Repeated use accumulates orphaned processes. Lower priority than blocking issues but valid pain point with confirmed user impact.

source_issues.title: The sdk should clean up mcp servers it launches on exit
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with reproducible steps. Launching chrome-devtools MCP server via claude_agent_sdk leaves browser open after session ends. Labeled 'bug' by maintainers. 4 comments indicate active community discussion. Resource leak every time MCP servers with UI components are used.

signals.topic: Linux musl/glibc binary auto-detection picks wrong variant causing query() to fail with misleading error
signals.summary: The SDK's runtime binary resolver prefers the musl variant over glibc on Linux systems. When both variants are installed (common with pnpm), it selects the musl binary which cannot execute on glibc systems, causing query() to fail immediately with a misleading 'Claude Code native binary not found' error. This affects both x64 and arm64 Linux environments.
aliases: musl vs glibc binary selection wrong
wrong libc binary variant picked on Linux
Linux binary variant resolver prefers musl
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm SDK runtime binary resolver picks wrong musl variant on glibc Linux systems (both x64 and arm64). query() fails 100% on affected systems with a misleading error message ('Claude Code native binary not found' even when the file exists). This is a complete workflow block requiring manual workarounds (passing pathToClaudeCodeExecutable explicitly). Regression from v0.2.113.

source_issues.title: v0.2.119 picks linux-arm64-musl variant on Debian (glibc) arm64 even when only linux-arm64 is installed
source_issues.evidence: query() fails immediately with error pointing at missing musl binary on a glibc Debian arm64 system where only linux-arm64 was installed. Regression from v0.2.113 native-binary refactor. Reproduced via Docker. Last known good: v0.2.76.

source_issues.title: Linux: musl binary preferred over glibc in v0.2.116 CLI auto-discovery
source_issues.evidence: On Ubuntu 24.04 (glibc 2.39) with pnpm installing both variants, the SDK picks musl first, causing spawn ENOENT with misleading 'Claude Code native binary not found' message. File exists but dynamic loader missing. Root cause: resolver iterates musl before glibc in the candidate array.

signals.topic: SDK forwards incompatible beta headers to Vertex AI causing 100% HTTP 400 failure
signals.summary: The SDK unconditionally attaches Anthropic-only beta tokens (effort-2025-11-24, tool-search-tool-2025-10-19, web-search-2025-03-05) to the anthropic-beta header on all outgoing requests, including Vertex AI which rejects them with HTTP 400. This makes every chat round-trip via Vertex fail completely with no user-configurable opt-out.
aliases: incompatible beta tokens forwarded to Vertex
signals.review_reason: Full workflow failure: every API call via Vertex AI returns HTTP 400. This is a complete block for any user trying to use the SDK with Vertex as the provider. The user explicitly reports 100% failure rate and had to disable CI paths.

source_issues.title: Vertex AI 400: SDK forwards `effort-2025-11-24`, `tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`, `web-search-2025-03-05` betas that Vertex doesn't accept
source_issues.evidence: 100% failure rate on Vertex-backed chat traffic. No public way to opt out without monkey-patching the bundled CLI. User had to disable affected paths in CI.

signals.topic: OTel telemetry emits Anthropic-native token attribute names instead of OTel GenAI semantic convention names, making cost attribution impossible in downstream tools
signals.summary: The SDK's claude_code.llm_request spans emit token counts under Anthropic-native names (input_tokens, output_tokens) rather than the OTel GenAI semantic convention (gen_ai.usage.input_tokens). Downstream observability tools (Langsmith, Datadog, Honeycomb) that follow the OTel spec see zero token counts and zero cost, making per-LLM-call cost attribution impossible from traces alone.
aliases: OTel span attribute name mismatch for token counts
gen_ai.usage token attributes not emitted in telemetry spans
signals.review_reason: OTel telemetry attribute name mismatch causes silent data loss: downstream tools see zero token counts despite actual usage. This blocks observability and cost attribution use cases that are core to the OTel integration purpose. User was forced to maintain a parallel local pipeline to capture cost data outside the trace, defeating the value of OTel-based observability.

source_issues.title: OTel telemetry: token counts emitted as input_tokens/output_tokens instead of OTel GenAI semantic convention gen_ai.usage.*
source_issues.evidence: Spans land with partial OTel GenAI convention (gen_ai.system and gen_ai.request.model are correct) but token counts use Anthropic-native names. Langsmith probe shows total_tokens=0, prompt_tokens=0, completion_tokens=0 even though the underlying API returned input_tokens=10, output_tokens=53. Per-LLM-call cost attribution from trace alone is impossible.

signals.topic: beta.sessions stream starvation — 4/5 parallel and even serial sessions fail with TypeError before receiving any events
signals.summary: When calling beta.sessions.events.stream(), 4 out of 5 streams fail consistently with 'TypeError: stream error: terminated' before any events arrive. This occurs even with serialized (single) session calls, ruling out concurrency issues. The standard Messages API works reliably with identical auth and model, isolating this to the beta.sessions lifecycle.
aliases: sessions.events.stream() fails with TypeError stream error terminated
signals.review_reason: beta.sessions.events.stream() has an 80%+ failure rate before any events arrive, confirmed across multiple controlled attempts over 24+ hours. This makes the beta sessions API effectively unusable for its intended purpose. The standard Messages API works as a workaround, but users relying on the sessions API face repeated silent failures. The isolation to beta.sessions (vs standard API) confirms this is an SDK/API regression.

source_issues.title: beta.sessions stream starvation — 4 of 5 parallel (and serial) sessions fail with TypeError: stream error: terminated before any events
source_issues.evidence: Controlled 5-attempt experiment across 24+ hours showing 80%+ failure rate (4/5 failures) on beta.sessions streams, including in serial mode. sawAnyEvent=false for all failures. Standard Messages API (client.messages.create) works reliably with identical auth/prompt/model, confirming this is beta.sessions-specific. Not rate limiting (no 429) or auth (standard API works). User had to rewrite against client.messages.create as workaround.

signals.topic: Non-interactive unsupported slash commands return a valid-looking session_id that cannot be resumed, breaking SDK session management assumptions
signals.summary: In non-interactive mode, unsupported slash commands emit a system/init message with a session_id and return a synthetic successful result. SDK clients commonly store session_id for future resume, but the session is never persisted to disk. A subsequent resume call fails with 'No conversation found with session ID'. This violates the SDK contract that session_id from system/init and result is resumable.
aliases: unsupported slash command returns non-resumable session_id
session_id from synthetic results cannot be resumed
beta sessions resumption fails for synthetic unsupported slash commands
signals.review_reason: The SDK emits a session_id in the stream that appears valid and resumable but actually cannot be resumed. SDK clients relying on standard session resumption patterns will silently fail with no indication that the session was synthetic. This is a contract violation that causes silent data loss for session continuity in headless/SDK integrations.

source_issues.title: Non-interactive unsupported slash commands return non-resumable session_id
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro shows: /status emits session_id in system/init and result messages, but no transcript file is created. A later --resume call fails with 'No conversation found with session ID'. SDK clients commonly treat session_id as authoritative for resumption; this silently breaks that assumption.

signals.topic: Composite action directory mismatch error causes complete action failure on every run (tsconfig.json fd mismatch)
signals.summary: Every triggered run of claude-code-action fails with 'Internal error: directory mismatch for .../tsconfig.json, fd 4' before any tool dispatch, returning exit 1. Users have disabled the workflow entirely as a workaround. Regression that appeared within a narrow window on 2026-04-26.
signals.review_reason: Main flow is completely blocked — every run fails with exit 1 before any tool dispatch. Strong user evidence: 10+ consecutive failures, workflow disabled as workaround, confirmed regression within a specific UTC window.

source_issues.title: Internal error: directory mismatch for ".../claude-code-action/<ref>/tsconfig.json", fd 4 — fails on every run
source_issues.evidence: 10+ failed runs across 2026-04-26 to 2026-04-27 on linxdigitalstudio-png/linx-edge-functions. Workflow disabled as workaround. Regression confirmed within a narrow UTC window on 2026-04-26.

signals.topic: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL environment variable ignored for internal SDK sub-calls, causing silent proxy billing for unauthorized Sonnet calls
signals.summary: Regression in v1.0.104/claude-cli 2.1.118. The ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL env override is honoured at top-level but ignored for internal sub-calls (task dispatch, planning, sub-agents), which send the literal 'claude-sonnet-4-6' model name. Users routing via OpenRouter proxy are silently billed for Sonnet requests they explicitly overrode with a cheaper preset.
aliases: Sonnet model override bypassed in sub-calls
signals.review_reason: Clear cost impact: users are silently billed for Sonnet calls they explicitly overrode. Smoking-gun evidence: actual proxy billing record showing Sonnet model despite preset override. Regression introduced in claude-cli 2.1.118 bump with clean baseline before.

source_issues.title: Action ignores ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL for internal Agent SDK sub-calls (regression in v1.0.104 / claude-cli 2.1.118)
source_issues.evidence: Smoking-gun OpenRouter record: actual 'anthropic/claude-4.6-sonnet-20260217' request charged to proxy key despite env override pointing to Minimax preset. 7 clean days on v1.0.99-v1.0.103, first leak day on v1.0.104. Quantified cost impact ~USD $1.16 over two days.

signals.topic: Native installer reports installation success while emitting 'claude command not found' warning — silent-success-mode bug causes next step to crash
signals.summary: In v1.0.106, the native install path reported 'Claude Code successfully installed' and 'Installation complete!' while simultaneously emitting 'claude command not found' warnings. The next step (Adding marketplace) crashed with ENOENT on the same path. The warnings correctly detected the failure but the wrapper treated install as successful. v1.0.107 (revert) addressed the specific version but the silent-success detection gap remains as a systemic risk.
signals.review_reason: Real CI failure with exit 1 caused by the installer reporting success while the binary was absent. The detection gap is systemic: any future installer regression producing the same warning state will fail the next step silently. Quantified window (~1h40min) but the underlying silent-success bug pattern is persistent risk.

source_issues.title: Native installer reports '✔ successfully installed' while emitting '⚠ claude command not found' warnings (v1.0.106 regression)
source_issues.evidence: Real run logs during v1.0.106 window (2026-04-25 00:16-01:56 UTC ~1h40min): install reported success, next step ENOENT'd and failed with exit 1. Issue filed by AdventureEd with full log excerpt. v1.0.107 partially addressed by reverting claude-cli version.

signals.topic: Bedrock provider: action sends deprecated thinking.type.enabled parameter to Opus 4.7, causing HTTP 400 on every request
signals.summary: The Bedrock path (use_bedrock: true) still sends the legacy 'thinking.type.enabled' parameter to Opus 4.7, failing with HTTP 400 'thinking.type.enabled is not supported for this model'. The v1.0.99 fix addressed the direct Anthropic API path but Bedrock users on Opus 4.7 remain completely blocked.
signals.review_reason: Main flow is completely broken for Bedrock users on Opus 4.7 — HTTP 400 on every request. The same issue was already fixed for the direct Anthropic API path in v1.0.99 but Bedrock was missed. Workaround forces model downgrade.

source_issues.title: Bedrock + Opus 4.7 still fails with thinking.type.enabled error (v1.0.107)
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 400 error on every Claude API call when using Bedrock with Opus 4.7 via Application Inference Profile. User-agent confirms action version. Workaround requires pinning Bedrock to Opus 4.6.

signals.topic: Agent mode silently discards session summary output on completion — clean PRs produce zero bot comment, breaking review automation
signals.summary: When running in agent mode (prompt: set, no @claude trigger), the session summary is generated by the SDK but discarded at action cleanup because agent mode hard-codes commentId: undefined. Verified across 7 PRs over two days: 5 clean PRs produced zero output on GitHub despite session success (cost $0.23-$0.49 each). Inline comments work independently, but the summary never posts.
aliases: PR review clean PR zero output agent mode
signals.review_reason: Core PR review automation use case is broken: sessions complete successfully and generate summaries, but output is silently discarded. Users get zero indication that review ran on clean PRs. Root cause confirmed in source code: commentId: undefined in agent mode skips the summary publish step.

source_issues.title: Agent mode discards session summary: cleanup phase gates updateCommentLink on commentId, agent mode hard-codes commentId: undefined
source_issues.evidence: Verified across 7 PRs over two days: 5 clean PRs produced zero bot output (no review comment, no issue comment, no PR review). SDK final output confirmed to contain complete 1098-character summary text emitted 117ms before result, but nothing reached GitHub. Root cause identified in source: agent mode returns commentId: undefined, cleanup skips updateCommentLink.

signals.topic: Security/policy systems incorrectly blocking approved user workflows or bypassing safety controls
signals.summary: Malware policy fires per-read blocking legitimate work; safety hooks are systematically bypassed with 125+ documented violations
signals.review_reason: Count=3 meets P0 threshold. Two distinct failure modes: (1) malware policy fires per-read blocking user-authorized workflows, (2) safety hooks are systematically bypassed with 125+ documented violations in one project. Both undermine the product's own safety guarantees — false positives block work, false negatives skip safety reviews. Main workflow is directly blocked.

source_issues.title: Malware-policy system-reminder fires on every file read in user's own project, blocking approved plan execution
source_issues.evidence: Malware-policy system-reminder fires on every Read tool call, not just once per session. Model treats the warning as an absolute constraint that cannot be overridden even with explicit user authorization. Blocks execution of approved plans in user's own legitimate project.

source_issues.title: Claude Code ignores its own safety hooks — violation #125
source_issues.evidence: Claude Code reads PreToolUse hook warnings (DANGER ZONE, HCC review, approach tracking) but treats them as skippable context rather than mandatory gates. Model proceeds with edits despite hook warnings. 125th violation in songwish-platform project.

source_issues.title: Claude Code ignores its own safety hooks — violation #115
source_issues.evidence: Same user, same project, same root cause as #54078. Filed ~1 hour apart, differing only in violation count (#115 vs #125). 125 documented violations in one project indicates a persistent systemic safety bypass.

signals.topic: MCP integration failures rendering external tool connections unusable
signals.summary: MCP servers (Supabase, Slack) either unavailable or returning corrupted data in Claude Code sessions
signals.review_reason: MCP integrations are core extensibility features. Supabase MCP unavailability forces users to fall back to Claude.ai web for deployments, completely bypassing the Code workflow. Slack timestamp corruption makes search unusable. Two independent MCP servers affected, both blocking real production workflows.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Supabase MCP missing from web/desktop Code workspace + stream timeouts
source_issues.evidence: Account-level Supabase connector works in Claude.ai CTO Console but mcp__supabase__* tools are completely absent from Code sessions across refresh, reconnect, fresh sessions, both web and desktop clients. Blocks Supabase-dependent deployments entirely.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Slack MCP slack_search_public returns corrupted timestamps
source_issues.evidence: slack_search_public returns mangled timestamps (e.g. 56310778-08-11) making date-based search unusable, while slack_read_channel/read_thread return correct timestamps for the same messages — proving the MCP formatter is broken.

signals.topic: Model delivers code with undetected logical errors and falsely declares tasks complete
signals.summary: Claude marks tasks done but code contains runtime errors and fundamental logic failures the model should have caught
signals.review_reason: Count=2 with 'consistently' language indicating systemic behavior. Model declares tasks complete but delivers code with runtime errors (dropped parameter names causing crashes) and fundamental logic failures (cache constant below minimum threshold). User cannot trust Claude Code's completion signal — every task may require manual verification, negating core productivity value.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Model hallucinating cross-project connections and refusing to load documentation before generation
source_issues.evidence: Model conflated three trading methodologies into one fictional framework, read wrong system card and reported it as correct, grabbed wrong project virtualenv to run a classifier, and produced incorrect code based on false assumptions rather than loaded documentation.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Claude Code consistently delivers code with undetected logical errors before declaring tasks complete
source_issues.evidence: Claude declares tasks 'done'/'passed checks' but code contains obvious logical errors. PR #15: LiteLLM fallback drops parameter names causing runtime failure. PR #16: Assumed ~40% cache savings but didn't verify the MINIMUM_PROMPT_CACHE_TOKEN_COUNT constant (2,181 chars) is below 1,024 token minimum — cache is never created. 'Consistently' indicates systemic overconfidence.

signals.topic: Stream idle timeouts during multi-step file generation in Code environment
signals.summary: Reproducible stream timeouts blocking file writes during edge function builds, forcing users off Code platform
signals.review_reason: 12+ reproducible failures in 5 days across multiple sessions is high frequency for a single issue. Stream timeouts block the deployment workflow entirely, forcing users off the Code platform. Scope reduction and fresh sessions do not resolve — not a transient issue.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Supabase MCP missing from web/desktop Code workspace + stream timeouts
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible stream idle timeouts during edge function file generation (~45KB TypeScript). 12+ failures across 5 sessions over 5 days (April 21–26). Failure at file write step after MCP source pull. Scope reduction and fresh sessions do not resolve. User forced to deploy via Claude.ai directly.

signals.topic: Context compression silently stripping credentials, environment facts, and ignoring user corrections
signals.summary: After context compression, model loses SSH credentials and architectural constraints, uses wrong credentials, and ignores verbal corrections
signals.review_reason: Context compression silently strips critical session facts including credentials and architectural constraints. Model uses wrong credentials leading to authentication failures. User corrections are ignored even when acknowledged verbally. Once compressed, there is no recovery path — forces full session restart with all context lost.

source_issues.title: Context compression causes model to lose environment facts, wrong credentials, and ignore in-session corrections
source_issues.evidence: After automatic context compression: (1) model used wrong SSH username that had never worked, (2) stopped accessing stored credentials/MCP tools used successfully earlier, (3) lost architectural constraints, (4) acknowledged user corrections verbally but continued wrong behavior. No recovery path without session restart.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin zombie bun processes accumulate unbounded, consuming massive CPU and causing MCP tool loss
signals.summary: Zombie bun server.ts processes accumulate over time (after ~3 weeks) — consuming 50-92% CPU each. The bot.pid stale-detection mechanism fails under wrapper-shell, allowing unbounded poller accumulation. After ~50 orphans, MCP handshake times out and tools silently disappear.
signals.review_reason: Long-running users accumulate zombie processes consuming massive CPU (up to 550% combined). When orphan count grows large, the MCP handshake times out and Telegram tools silently disappear mid-session — users cannot see that tools are gone since mcp list still shows Connected. This is significant resource waste AND key feature unavailability.

source_issues.title: [telegram] bun server.ts processes accumulate as zombies, consuming high CPU
source_issues.evidence: 6 zombie processes consuming 50-92% CPU each (~330-550% combined). SIGTERM ignored; only SIGKILL works. After ~3 weeks of use.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin: stale server.ts can spin at 100% CPU — SIGTERM fallback missing
source_issues.evidence: Orphan server.ts stuck at 99-100% CPU for hours. SIGTERM ignored because process is in a tight loop. No fallback to SIGKILL.

source_issues.title: telegram: orphan watchdog and stale-PID check both fail under wrapper-shell, allowing unbounded poller accumulation
source_issues.evidence: 73 live bun server.ts processes all polling the same bot token on 409 Conflict, combined CPU > 100%. Only one PID is tracked in bot.pid so others are invisible. After ~50 orphans, MCP handshake times out and tools vanish even though mcp list shows Connected.

signals.topic: Typing indicator expires before Claude response completes, making bot appear frozen
signals.summary: sendChatAction/sendTyping is called exactly once on inbound message. Telegram clears it after ~5s and Discord after ~10s. Claude responses routinely take 20s+. Users believe the bot froze.
signals.review_reason: For any substantive Claude response (deep research, complex agents, slow shells), the typing indicator vanishes after 5-10 seconds. Users consistently believe the bot has frozen or stopped processing. This is a clear and obvious experience degradation across both Telegram and Discord for the plugin's core use case.

source_issues.title: telegram: typing indicator only visible for first ~5 seconds of long responses
source_issues.evidence: sendChatAction sent exactly once on inbound message. Telegram clears typing after ~5 seconds. For responses taking >30s (deep research, multi-tool agents), the bot appears unresponsive for almost the entire wait.

source_issues.title: discord plugin: typing indicator dies before reply lands on slow Claude responses
source_issues.evidence: sendTyping() called once. Discord's typing indicator expires ~10s. Claude responses routinely take 20s+. The ... indicator dies well before the reply posts, so users assume the bot froze.

signals.topic: Allowlisted Discord bots are silently blocked from messaging despite explicit user configuration
signals.summary: messageCreate handler drops all bot-authored messages before the access-control evaluation. Bots explicitly paired via /discord:access and added to allowFrom are silently ignored with no error. This blocks multi-agent Discord team setups.
signals.review_reason: CI status bots, monitoring bots, and project manager bots are completely blocked from communicating even when explicitly allowlisted by the user. This defeats a core multi-agent use case for Discord integration. The silence (no error surfaced) makes debugging extremely painful — users see no indication that their explicitly configured bot was silently ignored.

source_issues.title: discord: messages from allowlisted bots are silently dropped
source_issues.evidence: messageCreate handler drops all bot-authored messages before access-control evaluates them. Even bots explicitly paired via /discord:access and added to allowFrom are silently ignored. No error is surfaced.

source_issues.title: [Feature Request] Add allowBots option to enable bot-to-bot messaging for multi-agent Discord team setups
source_issues.evidence: Multi-agent orchestration is impossible because bot messages are silently dropped even when sender's ID is in allowFrom. Root cause: bot filter fires before allowlist check.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin .env loader corrupts bot token on Windows due to CRLF line endings
signals.summary: On Windows, the Telegram plugin's .env loader splits on \n only, causing \r to remain in the token value. This makes the bot token malformed, resulting in API failures and misleading 'token required' errors.
signals.review_reason: Windows users cannot use the Telegram plugin at all — the bot token is silently corrupted and every API call fails. The plugin appears to configure correctly but is completely non-functional on Windows. This is a main flow block for the Telegram integration on Windows.

source_issues.title: [telegram] .env loader mis-parses CRLF files on Windows, corrupting TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
source_issues.evidence: On Windows, /telegram:configure writes .env with CRLF. The loader splits on \n only, so process.env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN becomes <token>\r. This causes grammy to build malformed URLs. The bot fails to start or fails on first API call. Confirmed on Windows 11 (bun runtime). Only workaround is manually removing \r from .env.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin drops reply_to_message_id, losing threading context in group chats
signals.summary: handleInbound discards the grammy context's reply_to_message_id field, so the LLM receives no threading context when users reply to specific messages in Telegram group chats.
signals.review_reason: In Telegram group chats, users routinely reply to specific messages. Without reply_to_message_id, Claude receives no threading context, making coherent multi-turn group conversations impossible. This is significant experience degradation for the primary group-chat use case.

source_issues.title: telegram plugin: drops reply_to_message_id from inbound channel meta
source_issues.evidence: handleInbound does not include reply_to_message_id in meta. ctx.message.reply_to_message is available in grammy's Context but is silently discarded. Without reply_to_message_id in meta, the LLM receives no threading context for replies.

signals.topic: README 中的 Browser Tools API Demo 快速入门链接失效（404）
signals.summary: README.md 中指向 Browser Tools API Demo 快速入门的链接返回 404，用户无法通过文档访问该快速入门指南。
signals.review_reason: 该链接失效直接阻断用户访问 Browser Tools API Demo 快速入门，是文档导航的主流程失败。虽然仅涉及单一仓库、单一链接，但影响明确：用户阅读 README 后点击链接被 404 阻断，无法继续学习/使用该功能，属于关键文档内容不可用。

source_issues.title: Documentation: Broken link in README
source_issues.evidence: README.md 中指向 Browser Tools API Demo quickstart 的链接点击后返回 404 page not found，截图证实的 404 错误页面，用户完全无法通过文档访问该快速入门内容。

signals.topic: pdf skill: IRS/现代表单解析崩溃导致主流程阻断
signals.summary: extract_form_field_info.py 在解析现代 IRS 表单（Form 8802、W-7、8821 等）及 XFA 风格 PDF 时，因 IndirectObject 未正确 resolve 而抛出 TypeError，直接阻断表单填充工作流的第一步。
signals.review_reason: 两个 issue 均来自同一用户在真实 IRS 表单填写工作流中连续遭遇的阻断问题，#1024 已在 2026-04-24 修复但原始 issue 证明用户首次使用即遇阻，#1025 同属 pdf skill 主流程命令；count=2 满足归并阈值，高置信度。

source_issues.title: pdf skill: extract_form_field_info.py crashes on forms with indirect /Annots references (e.g. all modern IRS forms)
source_issues.evidence: 运行官方 forms.md 文档中的命令即触发 TypeError: 'IndirectObject' object is not iterable；现代 IRS 表单（8802/8821/W-7）全部受此影响；用户首次使用即遇阻

source_issues.title: pdf skill: convert_pdf_to_images.py fails with FileNotFoundError if output directory doesn't exist
source_issues.evidence: 同 skill 第二个脚本同样在官方文档工作流中崩溃；错误信息不友好，无修复提示；同一用户在同一表单场景下连续遇到两个阻断问题

signals.topic: eval-viewer review.html 将非 ASCII 字符序列化为 \uXXXX 导致非英语项目评测报告不可读
signals.summary: generate_review.py 使用 json.dumps(embedded) 默认 ensure_ascii=True，将非 ASCII 字符全部转义为 \uXXXX；浏览器渲染时未反转义，导致俄语/中文/日语/德语等项目的评测报告完全不可用。
signals.review_reason: 关键功能（评测报告查看）对非英语用户完全不可用；有具体错误现象和受影响的真实使用场景；影响范围覆盖所有非 ASCII 语言用户；单仓问题但影响明确且严重。

source_issues.title: skill-creator: eval-viewer escapes non-ASCII text in review.html (review unreadable for non-English projects)
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确报告在构建俄语代码库项目 skill 时评测报告不可读；错误现象具体（контрактов 显示为 \u043a\u043e\u043d\u0442\u0440\u0430\u043a\u0442\u043e\u0432）；影响所有非 ASCII 语言项目（俄/中/日/德/法）；修复方案明确（ensure_ascii=False一行修改）

signals.topic: macOS 上 pack.py 将 .DS_Store 打包进 Office 文档导致 Microsoft Office 报损或拒绝打开
signals.summary: pack.py 未过滤 macOS 元数据文件 .DS_Store；打包后生成的 pptx/docx/xlsx 包含未在 [Content_Types].xml 中声明的条目；Microsoft Office 365 显示修复对话框或直接拒绝打开，LibreOffice 可正常打开。
signals.review_reason: macOS 用户使用 Office skill 生成文件后，Microsoft Office 端无法正常使用，工作流结果无法交付；影响明确且跨文件格式（pptx/docx/xlsx）；LibreOffice 不报错导致 CI 可能无法发现问题。

source_issues.title: pack.py bundles .DS_Store on macOS, causing Office to flag files as corrupt
source_issues.evidence: 用户实测：Microsoft 365 for Mac 中，打开含 .DS_Store 的 pack.py 输出触发修复对话框；删除 .DS_Store 后同命令产出干净文件；此问题影响所有 macOS 用户使用 pptx/docx/xlsx skill 处理 Office 文件

signals.topic: Provider-reported context limit is discarded, causing model overflow/crash for local models
signals.summary: Goose fetches max_input_tokens from the provider API but discards it and defaults to a hardcoded 128k limit. This causes local models with smaller context windows to crash or receive too many tokens, and breaks context compaction logic.
aliases: Context limit not respected from LiteLLM proxy
Local model context overflow due to ignored provider metadata
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm that Goose ignores the context limit reported by provider APIs and defaults to 128k. This directly causes local models (with smaller context windows) to crash or overflow tokens. It also silently breaks automatic context compaction, which relies on accurate context window tracking. This is a systemic issue affecting all non-default local model configurations, making the tool unreliable for a core use case.

source_issues.title: Context limit from Provider API is discarded, causing fallback to 128k for local models
source_issues.evidence: Goose fetches max_input_tokens from LiteLLM /v1/models endpoint but then discards it in the fetch_supported_models return value (only returns Vec<String>). Models with smaller context windows (e.g., 8k tokens for Qwen) receive too many tokens and crash. Context compaction at wrong threshold.

source_issues.title: Custom provider context_limit not reflected in Desktop UI — hard to change from 128K default
source_issues.evidence: Context limit defined in custom provider JSON is respected, but the Desktop UI shows 128k/128k even for models with larger limits. No UI field to edit context_limit; the only workaround is manual JSON file editing. Users of local/vLLM/Ollama models are affected.

signals.topic: DeepSeek V4 thinking mode breaks multi-turn conversations with 400 error
signals.summary: When using DeepSeek V4 with thinking/reasoning mode, multi-turn conversations fail with a 400 error because Goose strips the thinking/reasoning content from assistant responses when building message history for subsequent requests. The API requires this content to be passed back verbatim.
aliases: Multi-turn conversation fails with reasoning models
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking bug: multi-turn conversations with thinking/reasoning-enabled models (DeepSeek V4) are completely broken. Every follow-up message after the first turn fails with a 400 API error. Users lose full conversation context on every exchange, making the tool effectively unusable for this popular model category. Count=1 but P0 is justified because the user impact is severe, deterministic, and represents a complete failure of the core conversation loop.

source_issues.title: deepseek-v4 thinking mode error
source_issues.evidence: First turn works, any subsequent message in same session triggers 400 error 'The reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.' Users must start a new conversation for each exchange, defeating the purpose of multi-turn sessions.

signals.topic: CLI session immediately suspends on startup in Tilix terminal emulator

aliases: Goose session freezes on startup in Tilix
Process suspends in job control terminals
Tilix TERM variable causes session hang

The process enters a stopped state requiring manual 'fg' recovery, which is not intuitive for most users. The workaround requires environment variable knowledge and is not documented.

source_issues.title: Goose session immediately stops (backgrounded) on startup in Tilix terminal
source_issues.evidence: Tilix terminal emulator sends SIGTSTP after session init, appearing as 'Stopped' in shell job list. User must manually run 'fg' to resume. Workaround of 'TERM=xterm goose session' exists but is non-obvious. Issue reproduced on Arch Linux with Tilix.

signals.topic: Infinite web_search↔web_fetch tool loop bypasses LoopDetectionMiddleware, exhausting step budget without producing results
signals.summary: The agent enters a 200+ tool call loop alternating between web_search and web_fetch that the existing LoopDetectionMiddleware cannot detect. Since the two-layer detection only matches identical tool call sets (hash-based) or single-tool frequency (frequency-based), the alternating pattern produces different hashes each time and neither tool individually hits the frequency threshold quickly. This consumes the entire recursion_limit (default 100 steps) without reaching the synthesis phase, producing no final report — a complete main workflow failure.
signals.review_reason: This is a main workflow failure. The agent enters an infinite web_search↔web_fetch alternating loop that bypasses both loop detection layers and consumes the entire step budget (100+ steps), producing zero final output. The issue provides detailed root cause analysis and observed evidence (200+ tool calls, recursion_limit hit, no synthesis reached). This directly causes '主流程失败/阻断' and '关键功能不可用'.

source_issues.title: Bug: Infinite web_search ↔ web_fetch tool-calling loop bypasses LoopDetectionMiddleware
source_issues.evidence: Observed 200+ tool calls in alternating web_search↔web_fetch pattern; LoopDetectionMiddleware fails to catch it; recursion_limit hit (default 100); agent never reaches synthesis phase; no final report produced. Root cause: hash-based layer produces different hashes for alternating calls; frequency-based layer tracks per-tool count, so neither web_search nor web_fetch individually hits warn=30/hard_limit=50 threshold quickly.

signals.topic: Windows PowerShell 5.1 does not support && chaining, causing all bash tool execution to fail
signals.summary: On Windows, DeerFlow prepends 'cd <workspace> &&' to all bash tool commands, but PowerShell 5.1 (the default Windows shell) does not support && as a statement separator (only PowerShell 7+ supports it). This causes all bash tool commands to fail at shell parse time with '&& is not a valid statement separator in this version', completely blocking the agent's ability to execute any host machine commands on Windows.
signals.review_reason: This is a main workflow failure on Windows. All bash tool execution is blocked at shell parse time due to && not being supported by PowerShell 5.1. The agent completely loses the ability to execute any host machine commands on Windows, including running Python scripts and checking ports. The issue explicitly states 'Agent 完全丧失了对宿主机命令的执行能力' and '此底层阻断' cannot be bypassed by skill-level adaptations.

source_issues.title: [Bug] LocalSandboxProvider with Windows PowerShell: && chaining in command prefix breaks all bash tool execution
source_issues.evidence: On Windows 11 with LocalSandboxProvider + allow_host_bash: true, all bash tool commands fail with PowerShell parse error. All commands blocked at shell parsing stage. Agent completely loses ability to execute host machine commands. Workarounds fail (cmd /c also fails because && parse error triggers first, and /c is intercepted by security filter). Issue closed — confirms real user impact on Windows platform.

GPT, Gemini, and other providers handle the same tasks successfully. The failures occur at the final report generation stage, consuming significant tokens without producing any output.
aliases: Claude request fails on large documents
Claude token waste on failed requests
signals.review_reason: This causes '体验显著下降' and '明显成本损失'. Claude is a major model provider, and all its models fail consistently on complex multi-page tasks while competing providers succeed. The user explicitly reports wasted tokens (大量token消耗但无结果). Though count=1, the severity is high — a primary model provider is completely broken for complex tasks, and the failure mode is cost-burning with zero output.

source_issues.title: 调用Claude处理复杂任务失败

signals.topic: Sandbox host-gateway address connection failures cause LangGraph to falsely report sandbox startup failure
signals.summary: DeerFlow uses host-gateway address to access the Sandbox container, but this frequently fails to connect. LangGraph then incorrectly judges the sandbox as having failed to start, even though the sandbox is actually running and accessible via host IP + exposed port on the host machine.
signals.review_reason: Sandbox health check false negatives cause workflow interruption. DeerFlow frequently misreports sandbox as failed to start (when it's actually running), leading to workflow interruption. This causes '关键功能不可用' (sandbox is a core execution component).

source_issues.title: Feature: Sandbox add network parm and use inner container_name instead of host-gateway
source_issues.evidence: Using host-gateway address to access sandbox frequently results in connection failure. LangGraph misjudges this as sandbox startup failure. However, the sandbox is actually running and reachable via host IP + exposed port. This causes false negative sandbox health checks and workflow interruption.

signals.topic: Context window deadlock — model reports 1M but fails at 500k tokens, chat becomes unusable
signals.summary: GPT-5.5 reports a 1M token context window to Cline, but the actual limit is 500k. When context reaches 500k, Cline deadlocks: it spams checkpoint markers, rejects all subsequent prompts, and shows a misleading error message. No automatic recovery; only manual restore-to-checkpoint workaround exists.
aliases: Context deadlocked at half the reported limit
signals.review_reason: This is a high-impact deadlock that permanently breaks the active Cline session. The root cause is a mismatch between the model's reported 1M context and its actual 500k limit, combined with Cline's failure to detect and auto-compress before the overflow. The workaround requires manual intervention and is not obvious to users.

source_issues.title: gpt-5.5 fails when context reaches 500k, even though Cline believes the max context is 1M
source_issues.evidence: At 500k context tokens, Cline stops accepting new prompts, emits only '----' checkpoint markers, and displays a misleading model-capability error. The active chat is permanently deadlocked with no auto-compression recovery. Users must manually restore to a checkpoint before the 500k threshold.

signals.topic: Grok and other LLMs emit HTML-encoded characters in tool call arguments causing shell execution to fail

signals.topic: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware reject decision causes infinite interrupt loop — LLM retries rejected tool indefinitely
signals.summary: When a user rejects a tool call in HumanInTheLoopMiddleware workflows, the LLM receives ToolMessage(status='error') which it interprets as a transient failure, causing it to retry the same rejected tool call repeatedly. The rejected tool_call remains in revised_tool_calls so the LLM generates the same call again, creating an infinite loop that never terminates.
signals.review_reason: User-impact confirmed: human approval/rejection workflow is completely unusable due to infinite loop. When a user rejects a tool, the agent gets stuck in a cycle of retries that cannot be escaped. This blocks any use case requiring human-in-the-loop oversight, a key safety feature.

source_issues.title: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware: reject decision causes infinite interrupt loop — LLM retries rejected tool indefinitely

The rejected tool_call stays in revised_tool_calls so LLM regenerates same call. Docs state 'reject should skip without retry' but no mechanism prevents retry.

source_issues.title: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware: reject decision causes infinite interrupt loop — LLM retries rejected tool indefinitely

signals.topic: CompositeBackend missing route prefix validation causes silent data loss

When misconfigured, writes to wrong routes silently fall through to the default backend with no exception, no log entry, and no way to distinguish failure from correct behavior — resulting in silent data loss.
signals.review_reason: User-impact confirmed: misconfigured CompositeBackend causes silent data loss with no error or warning. This is a serious issue as users may not realize their writes are going to the wrong backend until data is lost or corrupted. While only 1 issue, the severity (silent data loss with no trace) warrants P1.

source_issues.title: feat(backend): validate CompositeBackend route prefixes at construction time
source_issues.evidence: Misconfigured CompositeBackend silently fails — writes to wrong route fall through to default backend with no error. No exception, no log entry, no way to distinguish failure from correct behavior. Root cause: CompositeBackend.__init__ accepts route prefixes that don't start with / or don't end with / without validation, despite documented constraints. Suggested fix: raise ValueError at construction time for invalid prefixes.

signals.topic: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() silently drops values after Overwrite — silent data loss
signals.summary: When multiple nodes write to a BinaryOperatorAggregate channel in the same superstep and an Overwrite(value) is followed by regular values, those regular values are silently dropped with no error or warning. This is confirmed as data-loss corruption during state transitions.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reporters describe identical silent data-loss behavior in BinaryOperatorAggregate.update(). Regular values appearing after Overwrite in the same superstep are silently discarded. This corrupts application state without any error signal, meeting the threshold for workflow_runtime pain point.

source_issues.title: bug: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() silently drops values arriving after Overwrite
