source_issues.title: BinaryOperatorAggregate silently drops regular values that appear after an Overwrite
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro: channel.update([5, Overwrite(10), 3]) → final value 10, '3' completely silently lost. No error raised. Language: 'Silent data loss during a state transition is dangerous.'

signals.topic: PostgresSaver.setup() / PostgresStore.setup() fails inside transaction due to CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
signals.summary: PostgresSaver.setup() and PostgresStore.setup() raise ActiveSqlTransaction when called inside an explicit transaction because MIGRATIONS uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, which Postgres prohibits inside transaction blocks. Breaks atomic provisioning workflows and multi-tenant onboarding.
aliases: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in transaction block
signals.review_reason: PostgresSaver.setup() unconditionally uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in MIGRATIONS, which Postgres rejects inside any transaction block. This breaks atomic provisioning (schema + checkpoint tables must commit-or-rollback together) and any upstream transaction context. The existing workaround (autocommit=True) defeats atomicity. This is a genuine workflow blocker for production Postgres deployments.

source_issues.title: PostgresSaver.setup() fails when called inside a transaction due to CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
source_issues.evidence: psycopg.errors.ActiveSqlTransaction raised. Breaks two legitimate scenarios: (1) atomic provisioning flows needing rollback-on-failure, (2) implicit transaction contexts from upstream LangGraph with non-autocommit Connection. Full repro provided using testcontainers.

signals.topic: ToolNode._arun_one blocks event loop when using sync wrap_tool_call — serializes concurrent tool calls
signals.summary: When a ToolNode uses a sync wrap_tool_call (no async variant), _arun_one calls it synchronously on the event loop thread. Since _afunc dispatches via asyncio.gather, this serializes all concurrent tool executions and stalls the event loop, eliminating parallelism benefits.
signals.review_reason: ToolNode._arun_one synchronously blocks the asyncio event loop when a sync wrap_tool_call is used. This destroys concurrency for all parallel tool calls in a single step, causing significant performance degradation. The blocking happens at the framework level, affecting any async agent graph using sync tool wrappers.

source_issues.title: bug: ToolNode._arun_one blocks event loop when using sync wrap_tool_call
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: _arun_one calls self._wrap_tool_call(tool_request, _sync_execute) directly on the event loop thread. _afunc uses asyncio.gather, so a single blocking sync wrapper serializes all concurrent tool executions and stalls the event loop. Confirmed with multi-tool async invocation.

signals.topic: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes caches INTERRUPT/ERROR writes, bypassing retry logic and CachePolicy
signals.summary: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes unconditionally persists task writes to cache. Unlike AsyncPregelLoop.put_writes which has a guard to skip caching when writes contain INTERRUPT or ERROR, the sync path is missing this guard. Combined with CachePolicy, failed/interrupted tasks replay error writes as valid results on retry.
aliases: cache policy replays error writes sync path
INTERRUPT ERROR writes cached without guard
signals.review_reason: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes caches INTERRUPT/ERROR writes without the guard that the async path has. With CachePolicy enabled, failed or interrupted tasks have their error state cached and replayed as valid results on retry, completely bypassing retry logic. This is a silent correctness failure that defeats retry contracts in production sync workflows.

source_issues.title: bug: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes caches INTERRUPT/ERROR writes (async path already guarded)
source_issues.evidence: Async guard exists at line 1407 but sync guard is missing at line 1203. Repro: graph with CachePolicy + graph.invoke() (sync) + trigger exception in cached node → re-invoke same inputs → error write replayed from cache instead of re-executing. Retry logic completely bypassed.

signals.topic: Regenerate from same checkpoint ID twice — second regenerate silently overwrites instead of creating new branch (regression in 1.1.7)
signals.summary: Since v1.1.7, calling astream twice with the same parent checkpoint_id (regenerate/time-travel) fails to create a second sibling branch. The second regenerate silently overwrites the previous branch instead of creating a new one. Regression introduced by PR #7498.
signals.review_reason: Regression in v1.1.7 where consecutive time-travel/regenerate calls from the same checkpoint silently overwrite each other's branch instead of creating new siblings. This is a main-flow time-travel feature that silently produces incorrect results. Bisected to a specific PR, and confirmed across 1.1.7, 1.1.8, and 1.1.9. The silent overwrite of application history is a significant correctness issue.

source_issues.title: Regression in 1.1.7 (#7498): Second regenerate from latest checkpoint doesn't create new branch
source_issues.evidence: Bisected: works on 1.1.6, broken on 1.1.7 (PR #7498). Repro: run 1 (1 branch), run 2 with same checkpoint_id (2 branches), run 3 with same checkpoint_id → still 2 branches, AI output silently overwrites branch 2. Root cause guess: eager fork checkpoint write on time-travel skips or overwrites instead of creating new sibling.

signals.topic: Dify Cloud plugin daemon fails to locate plugin runtime — all LLM nodes report 'model not exists'/'model schema not found'
signals.summary: On Dify Cloud, after clearing browser cache or installing certain plugins (GroqCloud, OpenAI), the plugin daemon fails to locate the plugin runtime, causing ALL model invocations across ALL app types (Agent, Chatbot, Chatflow, Workflow) to fail with 'model schema not found' or 'model not exists'. API keys are valid; the issue is entirely platform-side.
aliases: model schema not found all providers
signals.review_reason: This is a P0: count=2, confirmed on Dify Cloud platform, blocks ALL model invocations across all app types. Two independent users report identical symptoms. Root cause traced to plugin daemon not locating plugin runtime. Validated that API keys and models are correct — failure is entirely platform-side.

source_issues.title: [Dify Cloud] 'model schema not found' for ALL models across all app types — plugin daemon issue
source_issues.evidence: Fresh Dify Cloud account; GroqCloud plugin installed with valid API key; curl to Groq API confirms key is active and returns model list. Yet every model across all providers/app types returns 'model schema not found'. Groq console shows 0 API calls — Dify never makes a chat completion request.

source_issues.title: [Dify Cloud] All LLM nodes report 'model not exists' after browser cache cleared
source_issues.evidence: After clearing browser cache (LocalStorage, SessionStorage, IndexedDB, Cookies), ALL LLM nodes in all workflows (including newly created blank workflows) report 'model not exists' regardless of model provider or specific model selected. Verified valid API keys, incognito mode same result.

signals.topic: Plugin auto-upgrade silently fails — daemon returns HTTP 200 but never installs new version, leaving plugins on old version
signals.summary: The scheduled plugin auto-upgrade task calls the daemon upgrade endpoint without first downloading the new package from the marketplace and uploading it to the daemon. The daemon returns HTTP 200, but the async installation goroutine silently fails because the .difypkg file is missing. The failure is invisible from the worker side; users are unaware their plugins never upgraded.
signals.review_reason: count=1, single repo, but the review_reason provides strong evidence: this silently affects 'every auto-upgrade attempt for any tenant' with zero user visibility. The silent failure pattern (HTTP 200 + invisible goroutine failure) makes this particularly harmful — users believe upgrades succeeded when they did not.

source_issues.title: Plugin auto-upgrade silently fails: package never reaches plugin daemon
source_issues.evidence: Worker logs show HTTP 200 from daemon /install/upgrade endpoint; daemon logs show 'failed to get package file: no such file or directory'. Plugin stays on old version. Worker ignores the daemon result (_ = manager.upgrade_plugin(...)). Author states this affects 'every auto-upgrade attempt for any tenant; the feature has never worked end-to-end on its own.'

signals.topic: HTTP Request node serializes empty array [] as blank, generating invalid JSON and causing 400 errors
signals.summary: When using raw JSON format in the HTTP Request node, referencing a variable with an empty list [] causes it to be rendered as blank content in the request body, producing invalid JSON (extra illegal comma) and triggering a 400 parameter parsing error that blocks the workflow execution.
aliases: empty array null JSON http node
empty list causes invalid JSON http request
signals.review_reason: Single report but directly blocks HTTP Request workflow node execution — a core workflow feature. Empty array serialization as blank causes JSON format corruption and HTTP 400 errors. This is a clear data transformation bug that breaks the main workflow execution path.

source_issues.title: empty array recognized as null in http request
source_issues.evidence: HTTP Request node with raw JSON format; variable with empty list [] rendered as blank in request body, producing invalid JSON with extra comma. Triggers HTTP 400 parameter parsing error. Workflow request fails.

signals.topic: Conversation variable type picker is non-functional on main branch — users cannot select variable types
signals.summary: When adding a conversation variable in the workflow editor on the main branch, clicking the type dropdown has no effect. Users are unable to set the type for conversation variables, making the feature unusable in current main.
aliases: cannot select variable type workflow editor
signals.review_reason: Single report, single repo, but directly blocks a core workflow feature. Users cannot set variable types for conversation variables, making the feature non-functional. The bug is explicitly confirmed on the main branch.

source_issues.title: add conversation variable can't select the type
source_issues.evidence: User reports clicking the type dropdown when adding a conversation variable has no effect. Author confirms only the main branch is affected.

signals.topic: Service API lacks Human Input Node endpoints — paused workflows cannot be resumed programmatically, blocking enterprise integrations
signals.summary: Workflows accessed via Service API that include a Human Input Node are permanently stuck in PAUSED state. There is no Service API endpoint to retrieve the human input form, submit approval/rejection, or resume the workflow. Enterprise users integrating Dify with external approval systems (Jira, custom dashboards) cannot use human-in-the-loop patterns via API.
aliases: human input node service api missing
human in loop service api blocked
signals.review_reason: Single report, single repo. However, the review_reason documents clear enterprise impact: workflows are permanently stuck in PAUSED state with no resume mechanism, blocking production use for external integrations. This is a missing capability that makes a key Dify feature unusable via the Service API.

source_issues.title: Feature Request: Service API Support for Human Input Node (Workflow Pause/Resume)
source_issues.evidence: Enterprise user reports Service API can start and pause workflows correctly, but provides no way to retrieve the human input form or submit approval. Workflows are permanently stuck in PAUSED state with no programmatic resume mechanism. Impact stated: 'cannot use Human Input Nodes in production workflows accessed via Service API, which defeats the purpose of human-in-the-loop AI automation for external integrations.'

signals.topic: Embedding provider switch silently drops memory writes with false success response
signals.summary: When switching embedding provider (e.g. OpenAI→Gemini) via dashboard or API, pgvector table retains original vector dimensions (1536). Writes of incompatible dimensions silently fail — API returns 200 with a valid memory ID, but nothing is persisted. Data loss is completely invisible to users.
aliases: vector dimension mismatch on provider switch
silent data loss on embedder change
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss with false success response. Users believe memories are stored (200 + memory ID) but they are not. Diagnosis requires direct postgres inspection. Affects every non-OpenAI embedding provider. Clear reproduction steps, root cause identified in code.

source_issues.title: bug(server): switching embedding provider silently drops writes due to vector dimension mismatch
source_issues.evidence: API returns 200 with memory ID after POST /memories, but SELECT COUNT(*) FROM memories returns 0. GET /memories returns empty results. No error or warning in logs. Layer 1: embedding_model_dims hardcoded to 1536 and never inferred from embedder. Layer 3: dimension mismatch fails silently without propagating exception.

signals.topic: Reasoning LLM providers cause silent empty memory extraction with no error signal
signals.summary: When a reasoning/co-thought model (glm-5.1, gemma3:12b, qwen3-vl:235b, etc.) is used as the extractor, the LLM puts facts in 'reasoning_content' instead of 'content'. Mem0 reads only 'content', finds it empty, catches JSONDecodeError silently, and returns empty results with no error. Users cannot distinguish 'no new facts extracted' from 'extraction completely failed'.
aliases: silent extraction failure for reasoning models
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss indistinguishable from correct behavior. Users of popular reasoning models (gemma, qwen3, glm, minimax) get empty results with no error. Explicit root cause identified in code (main.py line 530-531). Multiple model variants affected. Workaround requires changing model, which is non-obvious.

source_issues.title: Bug: Reasoning LLM providers (glm-5.1, gemma3:12b, qwen3-vl:235b) cause silent empty extraction results
source_issues.evidence: glm-5.1, gemma3:12b, minimax-m2.7, qwen3-vl:235b-instruct all return content='' with reasoning_content containing the facts JSON. Mem0 reads only content, json.loads('') raises JSONDecodeError, caught silently → results=[]. Non-reasoning control (qwen3-coder-next) works perfectly. Caller cannot distinguish 'no facts found' from 'extraction failed silently'.

signals.topic: Dashboard saves wrong API key on provider switch and permanently locks out self-hosted users
signals.summary: Two bugs combine: (1) Dashboard pre-populates API key field with old provider's key when switching provider dropdown; if user doesn't manually delete it, stale key is saved to DB for the new provider, causing all operations to fail. (2) Once any config is saved to DB, .env values can never override it — users are trapped in unrecoverable broken state with no reset path.
aliases: stale API key saved on provider change
unrecoverable config lockout after provider switch
signals.review_reason: Complete workflow block for self-hosted users switching from OpenAI to non-OpenAI providers. Two bugs create unrecoverable lockout — user cannot recover via .env (documented approach) and error message gives no hint about root cause. Combined with pp-1, switching providers on self-hosted server is effectively broken.

source_issues.title: bug(server): dashboard saves wrong API key on provider change; .env cannot override database config
source_issues.evidence: Dashboard pre-populates old API key when provider changes; save writes stale OpenAI key for Gemini provider → 'INVALID_ARGUMENT — API key not valid'. server_state.py always merges DB overrides on top of DEFAULT_CONFIG → .env change has zero effect after first DB save. User is permanently trapped. Escape requires undocumented POST /configure via curl.

signals.topic: Historical observation timestamp ignored during memory extraction, falls back to current date
signals.summary: generate_additive_extraction_prompt() supports a timestamp parameter for Observation Date, but the call sites in _add_to_vector_store() never pass it. Historical timestamps in metadata are ignored, causing 'last week', 'yesterday', and 'recently' to be resolved against processing date instead of actual conversation date. This corrupts temporal context for any time-sensitive retrieval.
aliases: historical date resolved as current date
observation date not passed to extraction prompt
signals.review_reason: Data correctness issue: historical memories are stored with wrong temporal context, corrupting future retrieval. Time-sensitive queries like 'what did I discuss last week about X' will produce incorrect results. Clear bug with specific code path identified.

source_issues.title: Observation Date falls back to Current Date during memory extraction when historical timestamp is provided
source_issues.evidence: User passes metadata={'timestamp': '2023-05-24T10:00:00+00:00'}, but _add_to_vector_store() call sites do not pass observation timestamp → extraction prompt defaults to Current Date. 'last week' in input resolved against wrong date.

signals.topic: Memory deletion leaves dangling entity references, causing stale relationships and potential downstream errors
signals.summary: When a memory is deleted via memory.delete(), the memory itself is removed but no cleanup occurs for entity relationships pointing to it. Other entities retain references to the deleted memory, creating dangling pointers that cause errors in downstream processing, memory queries that reference deleted content, and graph traversal operations.
aliases: dangling entity references after memory deletion
orphaned entity links after memory removal
signals.review_reason: Data integrity issue: deleted memories leave dangling graph references that corrupt subsequent queries and graph operations. Clear bug with reproducible steps. Affects any multi-entity memory workflow.

source_issues.title: Memory deletion removes entity but doesn't clean up relationships in other entities
source_issues.evidence: Adding two memories with overlapping entities, then deleting one, leaves dangling references in other memory/entity entries. Downstream queries referencing deleted memory fail; graph traversal follows dead links.

signals.topic: Python: Foreach loop exits at first action instead of last, causing parallel instead of sequential execution of body actions
signals.summary: In declarative workflows, when a Foreach loop body contains multiple sequential actions, the loop advances to the next iteration as soon as the FIRST action completes, instead of waiting for all body actions to finish. The exit edge is wired to the first executor rather than the last. This silently corrupts workflow execution logic — actions run in parallel across iterations instead of sequentially.
aliases: foreach loop body not executing sequentially
signals.review_reason: Semantic corruption of core loop construct: workflow logic executes incorrectly (parallel instead of sequential) with no error raised, making it a silent but severe data/flow correctness bug. Affects all declarative workflow users with Foreach loops containing multiple body actions.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Foreach loop body: exit edge wired to first action instead of last, causing parallel execution
source_issues.evidence: Foreach loop body actions execute in parallel across iterations instead of sequentially. Root cause identified in _create_foreach_structure() — body exits wired to first action instead of last.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Foreach loop body: exit edge wired to first action instead of last, causing parallel execution
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report of the same Foreach loop bug, confirmed closed as same issue.

signals.topic: .NET: Declarative workflow and agent samples fail to compile, blocking user onboarding
signals.summary: Multiple .NET declarative samples (Agent_Step16_Declarative and CustomAgentExecutors) fail to compile due to missing packages or unimplemented abstract methods (ConfigureProtocol). Users attempting to evaluate or learn declarative workflows are blocked from running any working code.
signals.review_reason: User onboarding is blocked: multiple .NET declarative samples are completely non-runnable, preventing evaluation of a key framework feature. Users cannot learn declarative workflows through the provided samples.

source_issues.title: .NET: Declarative Agent Sample issue/question
source_issues.evidence: Declarative Agent Sample (Agent_Step16_Declarative) does not compile due to missing ChatClientPromptAgentFactory package implementation.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: Workflow Sample does not compile
source_issues.evidence: CustomAgentExecutors workflow sample fails to compile requiring implementation of abstract method ConfigureProtocol. Sample is non-runnable.

signals.topic: Python: MCP tool spans mis-parented — httpx calls in separate anyio task don't inherit span context
signals.summary: When MCP tools are invoked via AIFunction.invoke(), the MCP SDK's httpx HTTP calls happen in a different anyio task that does not inherit the parent span context. This breaks end-to-end distributed tracing for MCP-based tool calls — the trace is fragmented and the tool execution is not linked to the parent agent span.
aliases: OTEL spans not inherited MCP httpx
signals.review_reason: Observability quality degradation for MCP tool users: distributed traces are broken (MCP httpx calls not linked to parent span) and OTEL spans are missing cached token data. These are non-blocking but cause significant debugging and monitoring gaps for production MCP-based agent deployments.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: MCP tool spans mis-parented
source_issues.evidence: AIFunction.invoke() creates execute_tool span via start_as_current_span, but MCP SDK's httpx calls happen in a different anyio task that doesn't inherit that span context, breaking distributed tracing for MCP tools.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: missing cached tokens on OTEL spans
source_issues.evidence: observability.py _build_response_attributes only emits input_tokens and output_tokens, ignores additional_counts (cached tokens). OTEL spans are incomplete for cost/performance observability.

signals.topic: .NET: OpenTelemetry.Api 1.15.0 dependency vulnerability breaks CI pipeline and local builds
signals.summary: OpenTelemetry.Api 1.15.0 has a known moderate-severity vulnerability (GHSA-g94r-2vxg-569j). This dependency is pinned in dotnet/Directory.Packages.props, causing all CI pipelines and local builds to fail until upgraded to 1.15.3. Users cannot build or ship code without addressing this.
signals.review_reason: Known CVE with direct user impact: ALL .NET CI pipelines and local builds are blocked until OpenTelemetry.Api is upgraded. This is a shipping-stopper for any .NET user building from source.

source_issues.title: .NET: Upgrade OpenTelemetry dotnet version to 1.15.3
source_issues.evidence: Package 'OpenTelemetry.Api' 1.15.0 has a known moderate severity vulnerability, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g94r-2vxg-569j and this is breaking CI pipeline and local builds.

signals.topic: Python: Session isolation broken for workflow-as-agent deployments in multi-user scenarios (App Service / Container Apps)
signals.summary: When deploying a workflow-as-agent behind an HTTP endpoint serving multiple concurrent users, per-user session memory is shared across users instead of being isolated. Users cannot achieve both isolated memory per user AND preserved memory across that user's messages simultaneously. This is a fundamental blocker for production multi-user deployments.
aliases: workflow-as-agent session state shared across users
signals.review_reason: Core production deployment blocker: users cannot deploy workflow-as-agent to serve multiple concurrent users with proper session isolation. Memory leaks across user sessions in production is a critical data-privacy and functional issue.

source_issues.title: Python: Session isolation does not work as expected for workflow-as-agent deployments in App Service / Container Apps
source_issues.evidence: Users report memory appears to be shared across users when deploying workflow-as-agent for multi-user scenarios. Both attempted patterns (shared workflow instance + session IDs, and rebuilding per request) fail to provide isolated + persistent per-user memory.

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor 在生产环境中默认不启用沙箱，用户面临任意代码执行风险
signals.summary: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor 将 LLM 生成的代码直接写入磁盘并以子进程执行，无任何沙箱、文件系统隔离或网络限制。仅有的一次性 UserWarning 容易被生产配置静默忽略，导致用户在不知情的情况下以完整主机权限执行任意代码。
signals.review_reason: 该 issue 提供了具体的攻击场景和明确的用户影响证据：用户跟随文档示例使用 LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor 时，代码以完整主机权限执行，无任何运行时安全控制。警告仅在 __init__ 时触发一次，可在生产环境被静默忽略。此为已知的生产部署风险，而非推测性安全问题。

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
source_issues.evidence: UserWarning 在生产配置中（-W ignore 或日志管道过滤）可被静默吞掉，实际无运行时防护。用户跟随 quickstart 示例部署时会直接暴露于任意代码执行风险中。攻击场景：间接 prompt injection 诱导 LLM 生成恶意代码（如读取 ~/.ssh/id_rsa 并外传），完整系统被接管、凭据被盗、内网横移。仅有警告而非强制阻断，缺乏显式 opt-in 机制。

signals.topic: VSCode/Cursor IDE extension blocks test discovery due to connection timeout (ETIMEDOUT)
signals.summary: After Playwright package updates, the VSCode and Cursor IDE extensions fail to populate the test explorer with ETIMEDOUT errors, making the test extension completely unusable. Tests are not listed and no play buttons appear in spec files.
signals.review_reason: Both issues represent the same root cause: version incompatibility after Playwright component updates causes the VSCode/Cursor IDE extension to fail to connect, completely blocking the primary test authoring and execution workflow. This is a main-flow blocker with clear user impact evidence — test discovery is non-functional, and the extension is unusable.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Cursor IDE Extension stopped working with ETIMEDOUT
source_issues.evidence: After updating Playwright npm packages, Playwright Test for VSCode extension stopped working in Cursor IDE. Test panel shows no test tree, no play buttons in spec scripts. playwright.config.ts shows error: connect ETIMEDOUT. Disabling the extension resolves the config error.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: VSCode extension - error connect ETIMEDOUT while populating test list
source_issues.evidence: VSCode extension shows 'connect ETIMEDOUT' on import line of playwright.config.ts, Test Explorer reports 'No tests have been found in this workspace yet'. Version incompatibility between Playwright components confirmed by user.

signals.topic: WSL webserver startup causes 2-minute ECONNREFUSED wait, severely degrading CI performance
signals.summary: In WSL mirrored networking mode, Playwright's webServer health check hits the Windows Defender Firewall which silently drops packets instead of rejecting the connection, causing Node.js to wait the full 2-minute TCP timeout before starting the server. This adds 2 minutes to every test run in WSL environments.
signals.review_reason: Although only 1 issue is reported, the user impact is severe: every test run in WSL environments incurs a mandatory 2-minute wait before the webserver starts, directly degrading CI/CD pipeline performance. The root cause (WSL mirrored mode TCP blackhole) is well-understood and documented. This is a main-flow blocking performance issue with concrete, measurable cost impact.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ECONNREFUSED, PW waits for a 2 mins timeout to start a server in WSL
source_issues.evidence: Consistently reproducible in WSL Ubuntu with mirrored networking. pw:webserver health check hits Windows Defender Firewall which silently drops packets, causing Node.js to wait the full 2-minute TCP timeout (ETIMEDOUT) before starting the server. Every test run takes an extra 2 minutes. Logs explicitly show 'Error while checking if http://localhost:1315/ is available: connect ECONNREFUSED ::1:1315 +2m' before server starts normally.

signals.topic: page.route() with unbalanced glob braces silently aborts navigation, causing tests to hang or fail
signals.summary: When a glob pattern containing unbalanced `{` or `}` is passed to page.route(), the internal regex generation produces an invalid regex that throws SyntaxError during route matching. The navigation silently aborts with net::ERR_ABORTED and the test hangs or fails with no descriptive error message.
aliases: route glob unbalanced braces syntax error
signals.review_reason: This is a silent failure that blocks the primary test navigation flow. A malformed glob (common in URL patterns) causes the entire page navigation to silently abort with no actionable error. Users must already know to look at debug logs to diagnose this. The bug is confirmed with a minimal repro and root cause identified.

source_issues.title: page.route() silently aborts navigation when glob contains unbalanced { or }
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro provided: page.route('http://*/foo{', ...) causes page.goto() to hang then fail with net::ERR_ABORTED. Root cause identified in packages/isomorphic/urlMatch.ts: case '{' unconditionally emits '(' with no balance check, producing invalid regex '/^(foo$/' that throws SyntaxError at match time.

signals.topic: connectOverCDP sends malformed HTTP request target when HTTP_PROXY is set, breaking CDP connection
signals.summary: Regression in 1.58.0: when an HTTP proxy is configured via environment variables, connectOverCDP sends a malformed request target (e.g., 'GET /http://host:port/path HTTP/1.1' instead of 'GET http://host:port/path HTTP/1.1'), causing the proxy to return 404 and the CDP connection to fail entirely.
aliases: CDP over HTTP proxy malformed request
signals.review_reason: Regression in a recent version that completely breaks CDP-over-HTTP-proxy use cases. The malformed request target causes proxy-returned 404s, making connectOverCDP non-functional in proxy environments. This is a clear functional regression with confirmed root cause in HTTP env proxy handling.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: connectOverCDP sends malformed request target with HTTP_PROXY
source_issues.evidence: Regression between 1.57.0 and 1.58.0. With HTTP_PROXY env vars set, chromium.connectOverCDP('http://localhost:9222') sends 'GET /http://localhost:9222/json/version/ HTTP/1.1' instead of the correct absolute-form target. Proxy returns 404 and CDP connection fails.

signals.topic: locatorOrSelectorAsSelector emits unparseable selectors; unsafe variant throws raw TypeError/SyntaxError on malformed input
signals.summary: Two contract violations: (1) locatorOrSelectorAsSelector returns malformed selectors verbatim instead of empty string, causing downstream parseSelector() to throw cryptic errors; (2) unsafeLocatorOrSelectorAsSelector throws raw TypeError (undefined access) on malformed .nth() arguments and raw SyntaxError on invalid regex literals, leaking internal failures to RPC callers.
signals.review_reason: The parser throws raw uncaught exceptions (TypeError, SyntaxError) on user-provided malformed input instead of gracefully returning an empty string or a typed LocatorParseError. This causes crashes in debugController.highlight() via RPC with no surrounding try/catch. The bug is confirmed across 5 programming languages with a complete reproduction script.

source_issues.title: locator parser: unsafeLocatorOrSelectorAsSelector throws on malformed input; locatorOrSelectorAsSelector emits unparseable selectors
source_issues.evidence: Full repro script provided. 30 cases across 5 languages where locatorOrSelectorAsSelector returns selectors that fail parseSelector(). unsafeLocatorOrSelectorAsSelector throws TypeError on malformed nth() and raw SyntaxError on invalid regex literals. No graceful error handling — internal failures propagate to users.

signals.topic: RedisJsonCollection.delete() silently fails when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names is enabled
signals.summary: 当启用 prefix_collection_name_to_key_names=True 时，RedisJsonCollection 的 delete 操作发送未带 prefix 的 key，导致记录无法被删除且无任何错误提示，造成静默数据残留。
aliases: Redis JSON delete key prefix mismatch
signals.review_reason: 这是明确的用户痛点：delete 操作静默失败（无错误、无异常），数据持久化层记录无法被删除，且被识别的用户明确指出现有集成测试未覆盖此路径。属于主流程阻断（非致命但功能不可用），且有完整 wire format 证据和多仓一致性问题（同版本 RedisHashsetCollection 无此 bug）。

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: RedisJsonCollection.delete() silently fails when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names is enabled
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供了完整的复现步骤和 redis-cli MONITOR 捕获的 wire format，清晰展示了 upsert 时 key 带 prefix 而 delete 时 key 不带 prefix，导致 JSON.DEL 命中不存在的 key，返回 0，记录从未被删除。bug 为静默失败，无异常抛出，调用方无任何感知。

signals.topic: AzureAiAgent sample 无法运行，新用户入门体验阻断
signals.summary: 官方 AzureAiAgent 示例 sample 无法正常启动运行，新用户在按照文档上手时即遭遇阻断。
signals.review_reason: 官方 sample 无法运行是典型的新用户体验阻断场景。用户按照官方文档步骤执行即遭遇错误，属于主流程阻断，且有错误截图佐证。虽然 issue 较老，但标注为 stale 且最近仍有活动，说明问题尚未解决。

source_issues.title: Bug: AzureAiAgent sample unable to run
source_issues.evidence: issue 包含截图（error attachment），用户按官方文档步骤运行 sample 遭遇错误，issue 仍处于 open 状态，标记为 stale 但最近有活动。

signals.topic: ChatCompletion usage 对象仅反映最后一次 LLM 调用，无法进行准确的 token 计费
signals.summary: 使用 IChatCompletionService 进行多次 LLM 调用后，usage 对象只包含最后一次调用的 token 计数，导致用户无法准确核算总成本。
aliases: ChatCompletion usage object incomplete token count
token accounting across multiple LLM calls
signals.review_reason: token 计费错误直接影响企业用户的成本核算，属于明显的成本损失问题。用户明确指出需要 proper token accounting per customer，issue 有 12 条评论说明社区高度关注，close 后重新 open 表明问题持续存在。

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Chatcompletion usage object reflects only last LLM call even when multiple has been made
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确描述需要 proper accounting of tokens spend per customer，usage 对象只返回最后一条记录的 token 数，导致企业级成本追踪失效。issue 有 12 条评论，社区关注度高。

signals.topic: VertexAIGeminiChatCompletion 在模型一次消息中执行多函数调用时返回 400 bad request

signals.topic: MCP server processes leak and accumulate on Codex Desktop/CLI, causing process pressure and instability
signals.summary: Codex Desktop and CLI repeatedly spawn MCP server subprocesses without cleaning them up. On Windows, internal title-generation sessions attach the full project MCP stack and leak process trees. On macOS, duplicate STDIO MCP server instances accumulate over time (48→60 processes, ~2GB+ RAM). Additionally, MCP tool invocation regressed for local providers (Ollama/responses API) in CLI v0.117.0+. Together these make the app unreliable under MCP workload.
signals.review_reason: 3 confirmed MCP server process leaks across Windows/macOS/CLI. Cumulative effect: host-wide process pressure, RAM bloat (~2GB+), app startup stall, and instability for power users with MCP workflows. Additionally, MCP regression for local providers blocks CLI usage with Ollama/local models entirely.

Two configured servers spawn repeated process pairs over time. User must manually reap stale processes.

Relatedly, the GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark model becomes unusable when the global weekly limit is reached, despite having its own remaining quota. Both issues leave paying users stranded mid-session.
signals.review_reason: 2 issues from the same user, both confirmed as blocking paid users from accessing the service. Auto top-up is a paid feature that fails silently, leaving users without a recovery path. Combined with the silent API quota switch (issue #19861), billing/rate-limit logic is a major pain point.

This is an explicit consent/billing failure with measurable monetary loss, meeting P0 threshold despite count=1 due to severity and clear user impact.

User loses session history and must manually restart. The expected behavior (auto-compaction or continuation) is a core product promise for long-running sessions.

The issue provides reproducible steps, root cause analysis, and a proposed fix. While count=1, the bug is blocking (agent hangs completely) and affects a core SDK feature (MCP tool registration). The suggested fix (prefixing tool names with MCP server name) is non-trivial and requires SDK changes, indicating a genuine design gap.

signals.topic: Overly restrictive websockets<16 upper bound forces dependency isolation workarounds
signals.summary: The SDK pins websockets to <16, forcing projects already on websockets==16.x to either downgrade globally or maintain an isolated dependency set — unnecessary friction with no technical justification.
signals.review_reason: This is a dependency management pain point that causes real workflow friction: projects on websockets==16.x must maintain isolated dependency sets or downgrade. The issue provides clear technical evidence that the constraint is unjustified (only breaking change is Python 3.10 requirement, already satisfied). While count=1, this is a known anti-pattern that affects any project with dependency overlap — likely underreported.

source_issues.title: Relax websockets<16 upper bound
source_issues.evidence: Version 0.14 introduces a non-optional dependency on websockets>=15 and <16. The cap forces projects pinned to websockets==16.x to either downgrade globally or maintain an isolated dependency set. The only breaking change in websockets 16 is Python 3.10 requirement, which the SDK already mandates, so the constraint is technically unjustified.

signals.topic: HITL resume drops tool output when parallel calls mix approval-gated and non-approval tools
signals.summary: When resuming after rejecting interrupted tool calls in a HITL flow, previously executed non-approval tool outputs are silently dropped, causing BadRequestError on resume.
aliases: HITL parallel tool calls resume failure
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed main-flow bug in the HITL (human-in-the-loop) feature. When parallel tool calls mix approval-gated and non-approval tools, resuming after rejection silently drops already-executed tool output, resulting in BadRequestError and workflow failure. The issue includes a full deterministic repro and root cause analysis (state tracking logic error in hydrate_from_state). This blocks a core SDK feature (HITL approval flows with parallel calls).

source_issues.title: HITL resume drops tool output when parallel calls mix approval-gated and non-approval tools
source_issues.evidence: When a model issues parallel tool calls where some require approval and some do not, resuming after rejecting the interrupted calls fails with 'BadRequestError: No tool output found for function call'. Root cause: hydrate_from_state() incorrectly adds locally-created function_call_outputs to server_tool_call_ids, causing prepare_input() to skip items whose output should be retained. Full deterministic repro provided.

signals.topic: Async Responses structured outputs cause memory leak / OOM in long-running services
signals.summary: Using AsyncResponses.parse() with Pydantic models triggers unbounded Pydantic schema rebuilds due to unresolved TypeVars, allocating heavy Rust objects on every call and causing linear RSS growth until OOM. Also manifests as PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue warnings in production.
aliases: Pydantic serialization unexpected value in responses.parse
signals.review_reason: Confirmed memory leak with flame graph evidence: every responses.parse() call allocates unbounded Pydantic SchemaValidator/Serializer Rust objects without caching. In long-running services (API servers, agents) this causes progressive RSS growth until OOM — a clear service-availability failure. Cross-referenced with issue #2872 showing the same root cause manifesting as PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue production errors. Both issues share the same TypeVar resolution failure in _parsing/_responses.py. Count=2 meets the frequency threshold for P0.

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: Flame graph attached; RSS grows linearly with request count; process OOM in long-running server; root cause traced to construct_type_unchecked with unresolved TypeVar causing model_rebuild to always return False and cache to never populate

source_issues.title: responses.parse() throws a PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue error in v2.21.0

signals.topic: Responses streaming accumulator crashes with AttributeError when receiving response.output_item.added with item=None

signals.review_reason: Hard crash (AttributeError) in the SDK stream accumulator that prevents any application-level error handling. While triggered by a non-OpenAI provider, the Python SDK is widely used against OpenAI-compatible providers. The fix is a trivial one-line guard. Exception occurs inside SDK code before application-level recovery is possible, making this a genuine workflow blocker for affected users.

aliases: Cannot request rescan without GitHub Issue

signals.topic: Ajv schema compile() called per-invocation without memoization causes memory leak and OOM crashes in long-running gateway processes
signals.summary: sharedAjv.compile(schema) is called on every command/workflow-step/validate invocation without memoization or cleanup, causing SchemaEnv/run closures to accumulate unboundedly. In production, this causes process RSS to grow from ~710 MB to ~1.84 GB in ~3.5 hours, eventually exceeding V8 --max-old-space-size=2048 and triggering OOM crashes requiring systemd restarts. Six call sites identified across ask commands, llm_invoke, pipeline resume, SDK validate, and workflow file loading.
aliases: OOM crash from ajv compile leak
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed production memory leak with clear user impact: the openclaw gateway OOM crashes repeatedly (3 documented incidents in one week), requires manual systemd restart, and affects a core execution path used by every workflow/command invocation. The issue contains heap snapshot evidence, linear growth metrics, and multiple affected call sites. While count=1 prevents P0 under the default rule, the production crash evidence (repeated OOM, forced restarts) is unambiguous and qualifies as a P1.

source_issues.title: Memory leak: Ajv .compile() per call in sharedAjv leaks SchemaEnv/run closures
source_issues.evidence: Process RSS grew from ~710 MB to ~1.84 GB in 3h35m. V8 heap grew +114 MiB / +1.19M nodes with linear growth. Process hit --max-old-space-size=2048 limit, causing OOM crashes. Systemd killed process near 4 GB RSS on three separate occasions: Apr 16 21:23, Apr 19 23:57, Apr 23 09:46. All six call sites (ask.ts:9, llm_invoke.ts:372, pipeline_resume_state.ts:220, Lobster.ts:215, workflows/file.ts:443 and 1926) compile without memoization or release.

signals.topic: Authentication failure retry loop triggers gateway rate limiter, blocking reconnection
signals.summary: When token mismatch or auth failures occur, the reconnect logic retries every 1 second with no backoff, flooding the gateway with failed attempts and triggering its rate limiter. Once rate-limited, each retry resets the cooldown, making recovery impossible and filling logs with hundreds of errors per minute.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user-facing bug: the auth retry loop causes a gateway rate limit condition that is self-reinforcing (every retry resets the cooldown), effectively making reconnection permanently impossible until the rate limit window expires server-side. The log evidence shows hundreds of repeated errors per minute, indicating continuous user impact. This meets the bar for a user pain point: critical functionality (gateway connection/reconnection) is unavailable due to a logic defect.

source_issues.title: bug: aggressive retry loop on authentication failures triggers gateway rate limiter
source_issues.evidence: Log evidence shows auth failures retrying every ~1 second endlessly, triggering gateway rate limiter with 'too many failed authentication attempts'. The reconnect attempt counter resets to 1 on each cycle, so exponential backoff never kicks in. Issue explicitly describes flooding the gateway, triggering the rate limiter, and making the rate limit worse since each retry resets the cooldown. Fills log file with hundreds of identical errors per minute.

signals.topic: Gateway startup completely blocked (~5 min) by sequential npm install of 63 bundled runtime deps on every restart
signals.summary: On every gateway restart or crash, OpenClaw sequentially installs 63 bundled runtime dependency packages before the HTTP server becomes available, taking ~5 minutes. During this window, health checks timeout, all channels (Telegram, etc.) fail to initialize, and the gateway appears hung with no clear signal.
aliases: gateway startup blocking bundled runtime deps
HTTP server delayed by npm install on restart
signals.review_reason: Main flow completely blocked for ~5 min on every restart. Gateway health checks timeout and all channel initialization fails during this window. Users see a 'hung' gateway with no clear signal about what is happening.

source_issues.title: Gateway blocks HTTP server startup while reinstalling 63 bundled runtime deps on every restart
source_issues.evidence: Logs show ~4.5 min gap between '[gateway] starting...' and '[gateway] starting HTTP server...' Health checks timeout for ~5 min post-restart. Channels (Telegram, etc.) fail to initialize during this window.

signals.topic: MS Teams inbound messages silently return HTTP 401 after v2026.4.24/4.25 runtime-deps move — CJS dynamic import of jsonwebtoken returns incomplete named exports, jwt.verify is undefined, caught and swallowed silently
signals.summary: After the runtime-deps refactor in v2026.4.24/4.25, the msteams plugin's dynamic import of CJS jsonwebtoken returns a module namespace where named exports are incomplete. jwt.verify is undefined, throwing a TypeError that is silently swallowed, causing all inbound Bot Connector POSTs to return 401. JWT validation errors are logged only at debug level, so the failure is invisible at default log levels.
aliases: msteams 401 JWT validation failure CJS interop
jsonwebtoken dynamic import CJS namespace broken in runtime-deps
signals.review_reason: MS Teams inbound channel completely broken after upgrade. Every inbound message returns 401 silently. Full channel regression from a runtime-deps structural change affecting all MS Teams users upgrading from v2026.4.23 or earlier.

source_issues.title: msteams: every inbound Bot Connector POST returns 401 after 4.24/4.25 runtime-deps move (CJS interop)
source_issues.evidence: Every inbound POST from Microsoft Bot Connector returns 401. jwt.verify === undefined in the loaded CJS module. JWT validation error logged only at debug level, invisible at default log level. Outbound still works, masking severity.

signals.topic: Ollama provider routing fails silently — agent fabricates successful local-model responses instead of surfacing provider connection failure
signals.summary: When the Ollama provider is unreachable, OpenClaw does not fail explicitly. Instead the agent fabricates a successful response using the default model and claims the switch to ollama/qwen3.5:27b succeeded. Users receive plausible-looking but entirely synthetic responses with no indication that the configured provider failed.
aliases: Ollama provider unreachable but agent reports success
silent routing failure fabricates model responses
signals.review_reason: Critical reliability failure: system silently delivers fabricated responses with no error indication when configured provider is unreachable. Fundamentally undermines user trust and can lead to real-world decisions based on hallucinated data.

source_issues.title: Ollama provider routing fails silently — agent fabricates successful local-model responses
source_issues.evidence: Agent claims successful switch to ollama/qwen3.5:27b and generates response, but status shows fallback model. Provider was unreachable (WSL2 to Windows Ollama host). No error surfaced to user — synthetic successful response delivered.

signals.topic: v2026.4.25 regression: memory-core resolves embeddings API key from OPENAI_API_KEY env instead of the active provider's key, causing 401 and completely blocking the agent
signals.summary: Upgrading to v2026.4.25 causes memory-core to use OPENAI_API_KEY (set for a scnet.cn proxy, not for DeepSeek) for embeddings calls instead of the deepseek provider credentials. This produces 401 errors that completely block all message processing — the QQ bot receives messages but cannot generate responses at all.
aliases: memory-core 401 embeddings wrong API key regression 2026.4.25
signals.review_reason: Agent completely blocked post-upgrade with no workaround. Clear regression from v2026.4.24 where the same config worked perfectly. Memory subsystem blocks all message processing.

source_issues.title: v2026.4.25 regression: memory-core breaks agent by using wrong API key for embeddings
source_issues.evidence: Agent completely non-functional after upgrade from 2026.4.24 to 2026.4.25. Memory sync fails with 401 'Incorrect API key' for embeddings. QQ bot receives messages but cannot generate responses. No workaround exists.

signals.topic: OpenAI Responses replay bug poisons long-lived sessions on GPT-5.5/GPT-5.4 — session history gets malformed assistant turns (missing required reasoning items) causing persistent 400 API rejections
signals.summary: In v2026.4.25, when replaying session history for OpenAI GPT-5.5/GPT-5.4 via the responses API, malformed assistant turns cause OpenAI to return 400 rejections. Once a session is poisoned it stays poisoned until history is discarded. Both GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4 exhibit the same failure mode from two distinct replay gaps: commentary text being replayed into canonical history, and reasoning items with encrypted content but no visible summary being dropped during persistence.
aliases: OpenAI Responses API session poisoning GPT-5.5 GPT-5.4 malformed replay
signals.review_reason: Poisoned sessions are persistent and can only be cleared by discarding conversation history. Affects long-lived interactive sessions which are a primary use case.

source_issues.title: OpenAI Responses replay still poisons sessions on GPT-5.5/GPT-5.4 in 2026.4.25
source_issues.evidence: Stored session transcript shows assistant turn with msg_id but missing paired rs_id reasoning item. Later API request returns 400: 'Item msg_... was provided without its required reasoning item: rs_...'. Session stays poisoned across multiple requests until history is discarded.

signals.topic: WhatsApp Dispatch 连接成功后消息处理管道断裂（消息已读但无法触发执行）
signals.summary: WhatsApp Dispatch 显示"已连接"状态，但用户发送的消息被标记为已读（蓝色双勾）后，整个消息处理管道完全不工作——UI 无响应，不触发 LLM 执行，不回复消息。根因是 WhatsApp Web 实例与 interpreter 核心之间的数据桥接断裂。
aliases: WhatsApp Dispatch message processing pipeline broken
WhatsApp connected but not processing messages

source_issues.title: WhatsApp Dispatch connected but not processing or sending messages windows

signals.topic: 嵌入式浏览器窗口遮挡所有 UI 选项卡，导致选项卡切换功能不可用
signals.summary: 在 X11 和 Wayland 环境下（hyprland 和 XFCE 均复现），在应用内打开任何浏览器页面时，浏览器窗口会覆盖所有选项卡的内容，导致用户无法访问或切换其他选项卡，嵌入式浏览器与标签页系统存在严重的 z-index/层叠冲突。
aliases: Browser window covers all UI tabs
Embedded browser z-index issue covering tabs
signals.review_reason: 该问题造成 UI 交互体验严重下降：嵌入式浏览器遮挡所有选项卡导致选项卡切换实质不可用。跨桌面环境（X11+Wayland）均复现，根因为浏览器窗口 z-index 错误。虽然 count=1、单仓、核心解释器功能仍可用（未阻断主流程），但严重影响用户同时使用浏览器和切换标签的场景，保留为 P2 边缘改进项。
