source_issues.evidence: 在 hyprland（Wayland）和 XFCE（X11）两种环境均复现，浏览器窗口遮挡所有选项卡，选项卡切换功能实质不可用。

signals.topic: Uncaught tree-sitter QueryError crashes Aider during repo-map generation on certain language files (Julia, Python modules)
signals.summary: Aider crashes with an uncaught `tree_sitter.QueryError: Invalid node type` when generating repo-map for certain files (e.g., Julia files, Python files with `module` keyword at line 2), causing complete workflow blockage. Three confirmed instances.
signals.review_reason: 3 confirmed crash instances with full stack traces. All are uncaught exceptions that completely block the user's coding workflow — Aider either fails to start or crashes mid-session during repo-map generation. The tree-sitter QueryError is reproducible for Julia files and Python files with specific constructs. This is a clear main-flow blockage.

source_issues.title: Julia crashes aider
source_issues.evidence: Aider crashes with tree_sitter.QueryError: Invalid node type at row 2, column 2: module when processing Julia hello world file through repo-map. Full stack trace shows crash at repomap.py:302 get_tags_raw(). State: open.

source_issues.title: Uncaught QueryError in repomap.py line 302
source_issues.evidence: Aider crashes with identical tree_sitter.QueryError during repo-map generation on a Python file containing `module` keyword. Stack trace identical to #4867: crash at repomap.py:302 _run_captures(). State: closed.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ImportError in __init__.py line 78
source_issues.evidence: Aider crashes on startup with ImportError: libstdc++.so.6: cannot open shared object file. Separate crash type but confirmed uncaught exception causing workflow blockage on Linux. State: closed.

signals.topic: UnicodeEncodeError from model output surrogates causes repeated error spam and degraded experience
signals.summary: When LLM models output emojis, special Unicode characters, or surrogate code points, Aider fails to encode them and repeatedly throws `UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters: surrogates not allowed`, causing error spam during normal usage.
signals.review_reason: User explicitly marks this as the 'most annoying constant error' and reports it fires repeatedly during normal usage when models produce emoji/surrogate characters. Although only 1 report, the labeled 'priority' tag and the user's explicit characterization of constant disruption indicate a real, recurring experience degradation that blocks smooth usage.

source_issues.title: Most annoying constant error - UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 24407-24408: surrogates not allowed
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly labels this 'Most annoying constant error' and reports it 'constantly present' whenever models output special characters/emoji. The error repeatedly interrupts normal usage with stack traces. Label 'priority' confirms triaged as important. State: open.

signals.topic: Sensitive files (.env) added via --read are sent to model context and persisted in plaintext chat history without warning
signals.summary: Aider's --read feature allows sensitive files like .env to be added to chat context. Their contents are sent to the remote model provider and written to .aider.chat.history.md in plaintext, including API keys, database passwords, and secrets — with no warning or redaction.
signals.review_reason: Validated security finding with explicit reproduction steps. Sensitive credentials (API keys, DB passwords) are confirmed to be sent to remote model provider and persisted locally in plaintext without any warning. This is a clear credential exposure risk — once .aider.chat.history.md is written, secrets are stored unencrypted on disk.

source_issues.title: Sensitive files added with `--read` are sent to model context and persisted in plaintext chat history
source_issues.evidence: Validated retest confirms: `aider --read .env db_config.py` succeeds, .env secrets (DB_PASSWORD, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET, JWT_SECRET, SENDGRID_API_KEY) are sent to model and written to .aider.chat.history.md in plaintext with no warning. State: open.

signals.topic: Aider generates and commits code that reads user's SSH private key (~/.ssh/id_rsa) without warning
signals.summary: Through conversational steering, Aider can be prompted to generate and commit code that reads the user's SSH private key from ~/.ssh/id_rsa and stores its contents in application configuration, creating a credential-exposure risk with no warning.
signals.review_reason: Validated finding showing Aider can be steered to generate code that accesses and stores SSH private key contents without any warning. SSH key exposure is a critical credential risk — the key could be exfiltrated through the config object or debug output. Count is 1 but the security severity is high enough to warrant inclusion as P1.

source_issues.title: Generated code can read SSH private keys outside the project directory without warning
source_issues.evidence: Validated retest demonstrates Aider generating and committing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and stores content in config['SSH_KEY_BACKUP']. The same file also contained a debug output path that would print all config values including the SSH key. No warning was given. State: open.

signals.topic: Aider's built-in URL scraping path attempts AWS metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254) without private-IP or metadata guardrails
signals.summary: Aider's scraping feature automatically attempts to fetch cloud metadata URLs (e.g., AWS 169.254.169.254) when found in documentation, without blocking private IPs, detecting metadata endpoints, or warning the user.
signals.review_reason: Validated finding demonstrating that Aider's built-in scraping path (not just generated code) attempts AWS metadata URLs without any guardrails. In cloud environments, this endpoint can return credentials. The product's own code path — not just model output — is responsible for the attempt.

source_issues.title: Built-in scraping path attempts cloud metadata endpoints with no private-IP or metadata guardrails
source_issues.evidence: Validated retest shows Aider's own scraping flow immediately attempting http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ with no metadata-endpoint detection, no private-IP filtering, and no security warning. Also generated unrestricted fetch code and test scripts targeting the same endpoint. State: open.

signals.topic: Self-hosted LLM-as-judge with thinking capability causes cryptic JSON parse errors without actionable feedback
signals.summary: When using a self-hosted LLM (e.g., vLLM) as an LLM-as-judge with thinking capability via OpenAI-compatible API, promptfoo attempts to parse thinking content as JSON, resulting in 'Could not parse JSON' errors with no indication of the problematic content. Users must manually add `showThinking: false` without any guidance or warning.
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow runtime issue: self-hosted LLM judges with thinking capability (common in vLLM deployments) silently fail test evaluation with cryptic JSON parse errors, providing no diagnostic information about what content caused the failure. Users cannot trust their judge evaluations without manual intervention. The issue is a real, reproducible failure path in the main evaluation workflow, not a hypothetical security concern.

source_issues.title: Improve Documentation : OpenAI compatible API
source_issues.evidence: User reports 'promptfoo will try to parse the json starting with the thinking content, which most often lead to errors ("string" or "Could not parse Json"). This was quite hard to debug since promptfoo doesn't show the string it was trying to parse.' Config workaround (add showThinking: false) is undocumented.

signals.topic: Judge provider config in assert/provider is silently ignored with no warning
signals.summary: When users define the judge provider configuration in the assert/provider section of YAML, the configuration is silently ignored. The configured self-hosted endpoint is not used, and the tool falls back to global defaults, leading to API calls hitting the wrong endpoint without any error or warning.
signals.review_reason: This is a UX/configuration silent failure: the judge provider config in assert/provider is completely ignored without any warning or error, causing API calls to go to unexpected default endpoints. This leads to incorrect evaluations running against the wrong judge and potential cost/accuracy issues. Users only discover the problem by noticing evaluations run differently than expected, with no diagnostic information from promptfoo.

source_issues.title: Improve Documentation : OpenAI compatible API
source_issues.evidence: User states 'I ended up declaring the full config in the defaultTest/options/provider but also adding this id in the assert/provider. As a result my config was silently ignored and I could only set the url and apikey through global var env.' No error or warning is raised when the assert/provider config is overridden.

signals.topic: Empty/invalid bug report template submission noise
signals.summary: A GitHub issue was submitted with a placeholder title (numeric string) and an empty bug report template, providing no usable information for triaging or fixing any actual problem.
signals.review_reason: This is noise issue data with no actionable content. The issue provides zero usable information for identifying any user pain. It is included here to formally exclude it from meaningful pain point analysis, as required by the hard constraint that all issues must be reviewed and the count field must reflect actual data.

source_issues.evidence: Issue title is a numeric string '853403640', body contains only the default bug report template with no filled-in details, no reproduction steps, no expected behavior, and no system info.

signals.topic: RedisVectorStore add/async_add returns corrupted node IDs due to incorrect string prefix removal
signals.summary: RedisVectorStore uses Python `.strip()` instead of `.removeprefix()` when returning node IDs, which removes individual characters from UUIDs instead of the exact prefix. Node IDs starting with characters present in the prefix (e.g., 'e' in 'semantic_cache_doc') get corrupted, causing data integrity failures and broken up/delete operations.
aliases: Redis vector store node ID corruption
signals.review_reason: Data corruption bug that silently breaks node ID integrity in RedisVectorStore. The corrupted IDs cause delete/update operations to fail silently since wrong IDs are passed to Redis. Has clear reproduction script with concrete before/after UUID comparison.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: RedisVectorStore returns corrupted node IDs in add/async_add due to misuse of .strip()
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction script shows `e7b95ae7-6369-404d-8287-1f4504121563` becomes `7b95ae7-6369-404d-8287-1f4504121563` (leading 'e' stripped). Affects all nodes with UUIDs starting with hex chars present in the prefix.

signals.topic: Node.hash uses MetadataMode.ALL causing silent unnecessary re-embeddings on every file modification
signals.summary: Since PR #18303, Node.hash includes all metadata via MetadataMode.ALL, which ignores excluded_embed_metadata_keys. File-stat metadata (mtime, ctime) from SimpleDirectoryReader is included in the hash. Any file touch/modification triggers a full re-embed cycle on the next ingestion run, even when text content is byte-identical. This silently multiplies embedding API costs.
aliases: IngestionPipeline unnecessary re-embedding on mtime change
Silent embedding cost multiplication due to file metadata hash changes
signals.review_reason: Direct financial impact: every production deployment with scheduled SimpleDirectoryReader ingestion over local files silently re-embeds the entire corpus on every cross-day modification cycle. Cost scales with corpus size and re-indexing frequency. The trigger is completely silent with no warning. Production data-loss risk if hash collisions cause wrong documents to be skipped.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Node.hash uses MetadataMode.ALL, causing unnecessary re-embeds when volatile file-stat metadata changes
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction script shows embed count doubles after a single `touch` on unchanged content. Verified with a counting embedder. External repo (stirelli/llamaindex-embedding-churn) provides 5-level progressive evidence including cost confirmation via real OpenAI API calls.

signals.topic: QueryFusionRetriever silently ignores retriever_weights in reciprocal_rank fusion mode
signals.summary: QueryFusionRetriever's `_reciprocal_rerank_fusion()` method does not apply `retriever_weights` even when explicitly provided. It always uses weight 1.0 for all retrievers. A weight of 0.0 (meant to fully exclude a retriever) is silently ignored, causing unexpected documents to appear in results.
signals.review_reason: Behavioral correctness bug: retriever_weights is a public API parameter that users rely on to control retrieval priority, yet it is silently ignored in one of the two fusion modes. This causes incorrect retrieval results that appear correct to users, making it a silent correctness failure.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: QueryFusionRetriever ignores `retriever_weights` when `mode="reciprocal_rerank"`
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction script: retriever_weights=[1.0, 0.0] with 2 retrievers returns ['node_A', 'node_C'] instead of expected ['node_A', 'node_B']. Second retriever (weight 0.0) still contributes node_C to results.

signals.topic: TreeSelectLeafRetriever query path returns empty source_nodes, breaking citation and provenance features
signals.summary: TreeSelectLeafRetriever's `_query()` method explicitly returns `source_nodes=[]` with a TODO comment, discarding all retrieved leaf nodes. This breaks all downstream features that depend on source attribution: citation rendering, answer provenance debugging, and any consumer checking response.source_nodes.
signals.review_reason: Key feature breakage: source_nodes is essential for RAG answer attribution, citation UIs, and evaluation pipelines. The bug has an explicit TODO in the code marking it as known, meaning it has existed for a significant time with no resolution.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: TreeSelectLeafRetriever query path returns empty source_nodes
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction script demonstrates that querying TreeSelectLeafRetriever returns Response with source_nodes=0 length, even when valid leaf nodes were traversed. Affects citation features, evaluation/debug workflows, and any downstream integration expecting source node visibility.

signals.topic: LLMChatEndEvent.model_dump() mutates ChatResponse.raw in-place, causing AttributeError in StructuredLLM users with OpenTelemetry
signals.summary: When OpenTelemetry (or any LlamaIndex dispatcher subscriber) is active, LLMChatEndEvent.model_dump() converts ChatResponse.raw from a Pydantic model to a plain dict in-place. Any subsequent access to the structured response object by the calling code raises AttributeError because .dict has no Pydantic model attributes.
signals.review_reason: Production crash in StructuredLLM workflows with OpenTelemetry instrumentation: users' agent logic fails with AttributeError after the LLM call completes successfully. The corruption is silent (works without telemetry, breaks with it) making it a particularly insidious bug that only manifests in monitored production environments.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: LLMChatEndEvent.model_dump() mutates ChatResponse.raw in-place, corrupting caller's response object
source_issues.evidence: Real production error traceback: 'dict' object has no attribute 'ruleset_id' in a StructuredLLM workflow using LlamaIndexOpenTelemetry. The bug is triggered by telemetry registration and causes silent corruption (dict instead of Pydantic model) followed by AttributeError at call site.

signals.topic: daemon start silently dies on Windows due to ps -o incompatibility and detached spawn issues
signals.summary: On Windows Git Bash, daemon reports 'started' but exits within ~2s; caused by ps -o flag incompatibility and detached:false on Windows.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking on Windows: daemon cannot stay running. Two independent reports confirm persistent issue across multiple Windows environments and Node versions. review_reason overrides default P0 threshold: count=2 is below P0 threshold of count>=3, so P1. But severity remains high as daemon is core infrastructure.

source_issues.title: daemon start silently dies on Windows due to ps -o incompatibility
source_issues.evidence: On Windows Git Bash, daemon reports '[OK] Daemon started' but exits within ~2s. ps: unknown option -- o. daemon.log stays 0 bytes. Workaround: daemon start --foreground works but still backgrounds.

source_issues.title: Daemon dies immediately on Windows + Node 25 (unsettled top-level await + detached spawn)
source_issues.evidence: Daemon uses unsettled top-level await which Node 25 detects and kills with exit code 13. Also detached:false on Windows means child dies when parent exits. shell:true makes child.pid be shell PID not node PID.

signals.topic: session save crashes with TypeError on undefined agentCount + session list shows corrupt Invalid Date rows
signals.summary: session save prints 'saved' then 'Failed' TypeError; session list renders broken table with empty rows and Invalid Date timestamps.
signals.review_reason: Data integrity loss + feature unavailability: session persistence broken with TypeError crashes. Corrupt rows accumulate and can't be cleaned — no valid ID to target session delete. Count=2 below P0 threshold; downgraded to P1. Severity is high: session save/list are core workflows for any user without pre-initialized swarm.

source_issues.title: session save crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading agentCount)'; session list shows corrupt Invalid Date rows
source_issues.evidence: session save prints 'Session saved' then 'Failed to save session' TypeError. session list shows rows with empty ID, empty name '-', and 'Invalid Date In...' timestamps. swarm metrics object undefined when no swarm initialized.

source_issues.title: CLI v3.5.80: session-end hang, session save TypeError, session list broken rendering
source_issues.evidence: session-end hangs indefinitely after writing state file. session save TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading agentCount). session list renders broken table with 10 empty rows and Invalid Date. Session summary shows undefined counters.

signals.topic: CLI commands hang after producing output: ruflo status / memory list / neural status never exit cleanly (teardown hang)
signals.summary: Three CLI commands print correct output but hang forever instead of exiting, requiring SIGTERM to recover.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: commands produce correct output but never exit, forcing users to use timeout or SIGTERM to recover. Count=1 prevents P0 classification, but impact is significant for any automation or CI scripts using these commands, as they stall indefinitely.

source_issues.title: CLI teardown hang: status / memory list / neural status print output but never exit
source_issues.evidence: Affected commands print full correct output then hang indefinitely. timeout 20s returns exit code 124 (killed). User must SIGTERM/Ctrl-C to recover. All three commands (ruflo status, ruflo memory list, ruflo neural status) affected consistently.

signals.topic: guidance ab-test feature produces zero-delta results due to default executor inability to swap CLAUDE.md between configs
signals.summary: DefaultHeadlessExecutor cannot isolate Config A from on-disk CLAUDE.md, guaranteeing zero delta between A/B configs.
signals.review_reason: Clear cost loss: ~$23 per benchmark run produces architecturally guaranteed zero-delta results. Feature advertised to compare CLAUDE.md configs is non-functional with default executor. User wastes significant money and time on meaningless benchmarks.

source_issues.title: guidance ab-test: default executor cannot swap CLAUDE.md between Config A/B (zero-delta by design)
source_issues.evidence: DefaultHeadlessExecutor reads on-disk CLAUDE.md for both configs, guaranteeing zero delta. Cost: ~$23 per benchmark (40 calls x 2 configs x 20 tasks), ~21 min wall clock, producing meaningless results. User cannot work around without implementing a custom content-aware executor.

signals.topic: guidance subcommand short flags (-t, -c) silently ignored on lazy-registered commands
signals.summary: Parser breaks out of walk when hitting lazy command name, preventing subcommand-level short alias building.
signals.review_reason: UX degradation: documented short flags (-t, -c) silently fail, causing user confusion. Workaround exists (long-form flags), reducing severity to P2. Low frequency impact.

source_issues.title: guidance: subcommand short flags (-t, -c) ignored on lazy-registered commands
source_issues.evidence: ruflo guidance retrieve -t fails with 'Required option missing: --task'. Parser breaks out of walk when hitting lazy command name. Workaround: use --task long form.

signals.topic: CLI `wait --download <path>` reports success metadata but saves file to wrong location (default ~/Downloads)
signals.summary: When using `wait --download <requested_path>`, the JSON response claims `savedFilePath === <requested_path>` and the file appears to be saved there, but the actual file is written to `~/Downloads/` with the original download filename. This silently breaks the file persistence contract and causes downstream wrappers to have incorrect file locations.
signals.review_reason: This is a silent file-persistence failure. The API reports success with correct-looking metadata, but the file is not at the promised path. Downstream wrappers that trust the response will get wrong file locations or missing files, making automation unreliable. This meets the bar of 'key functional contract broken with no error signal'.

source_issues.title: wait --download <path> reports requested path but saves to default Downloads directory
source_issues.evidence: JSON metadata claims `savedFilePath === /tmp/<unique>/wait-download-report.txt` but file appears under `~/Downloads/pi-agent-browser-wait-download-contract.txt`. Downstream wrappers cannot rely on `savedFilePath` as verified persistence.

signals.topic: `--headed` window is killed and Chrome is relaunched on every CLI invocation (macOS 26)
signals.summary: On macOS 26, every CLI command sent to a `--headed` daemon causes the entire Chrome process tree to be killed and a new Chrome relaunched in headless mode. The visible window disappears within ~1 second. Without `--profile`, page state is lost (URL becomes `about:blank`). With `--profile`, the page state survives but the kill+relaunch still happens. This affects both agent-browser 0.25.3 and 0.26.0.
aliases: headed mode kills chrome every command macOS
headed window disappears on CLI command
signals.review_reason: This is a high-severity main-flow break. Every single CLI command invocation to a `--headed` session kills the browser process and relaunches, making headed mode fundamentally broken on macOS 26. The user loses window state and page context on every command. The workaround does not fix the underlying kill/relaunch cycle. P0 due to complete headed-mode breakage across macOS 26.

source_issues.title: `--headed` window dies and Chrome is killed+relaunched on every CLI invocation (macOS 26 / Darwin 25.x)
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible on macOS 26 / Darwin 25.4.0 with Chrome for Testing 147. Every `agent-browser` CLI invocation (e.g. `agent-browser get url`) triggers full Chrome process tree kill and relaunch. PIDs change between every snapshot. The workaround of setting `AGENT_BROWSER_HEADED=true` does not prevent the kill+relaunch, only reopens headed mode.

signals.topic: Browser state (auth cookies) from `config.json` fails to persist session; tab auto-closes during operations
signals.summary: When `state` path is set in `~/.agent-browser/config.json`, loading the saved auth cookies fails to restore the session correctly. The browser appears to open successfully, but when subsequent commands like `get text` are run, the tab is silently closed and elements cannot be found. Removing the `config.json` and passing `--state` as a CLI flag works as expected, indicating a config file parsing issue.
aliases: session cookie auth not restored from config file
signals.review_reason: Auth cookie restoration from config.json is a core use case for agentic browser automation. When it silently fails (tab auto-closes with no error), users cannot reliably maintain authenticated sessions across commands. This blocks the primary session persistence workflow and forces a CLI flag workaround. Explicit user impact: session state loss, workflow breakdown.

source_issues.title: state does not work in the way config.json
source_issues.evidence: With `~/.agent-browser/config.json` containing `"state": "xxxx/my-auth.json"`, `agent-browser open` succeeds but `agent-browser get text main` fails with 'Element not found' and the tab is observed auto-closing. Same auth file works when passed as `--state` flag. Regression from expected behavior.

signals.topic: Redirect links and new tab opening fail in headless mode
signals.summary: In headless mode (without `--headed`), redirect links that open in new tabs do not appear when `agent-browser tab` is run. The same redirects work correctly in headed mode with automatic focus shift to new tabs. This is a functional gap between headed and headless modes that breaks automation workflows relying on redirect-based navigation in headless environments.
aliases: new tabs not detected in headless mode
signals.review_reason: Headless mode is critical for CI/CD and server-side automation. When redirect-based navigation silently fails to detect new tabs, automated workflows break without clear error signals. The feature works in headed mode but not headless, creating a significant mode-specific regression that blocks headless-first users.

source_issues.title: Redirects don't work or new tabs don't show up when agent-browser is used in headless mode
source_issues.evidence: Links with redirects that open new tabs do not appear in `agent-browser tab` output in headless mode. Same flow in headed mode correctly detects new tabs and shifts focus. This is a behavioral inconsistency between headed and headless modes.

signals.topic: `state load` command hangs and fails with 'Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)'
signals.summary: After saving login cookies with `state save`, loading them with `state load` hangs with no response for a long time and then fails with error 'Failed to read: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35) (after 5 retries - daemon may be busy or unresponsive)'. This is a regression — the same workflow worked in earlier versions but fails in 0.26.0.
signals.review_reason: This is a regression in session restoration functionality. The `state save` → `state load` workflow is a core use case for maintaining authenticated sessions. The failure with a specific OS error code (35) after a long hang, combined with the explicit regression claim, indicates a real user-impacting bug. Users cannot reload their saved auth sessions.

source_issues.title: Executing the command agent-browser state load login.json takes a long time with no response and eventually fails?
source_issues.evidence: After `state save ./login.json` succeeds, `state load ./login.json` hangs indefinitely then fails with 'Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)' after 5 retries. Reporter explicitly states 'this issue did not exist in earlier versions; it fails directly in the latest version'. Affects session restoration workflow.

signals.topic: File media type detection and allowlist broken — m4a misdetected as wav, custom file types rejected, base64 assumption too rigid
signals.summary: The SDK's file media type handling is broken in three interconnected ways: (1) experimental_transcribe checks for the 'ftyp' box header at byte offset 0 but m4a/mp4 files written by iOS, Android, ffmpeg, and ElevenLabs have it at offset 4, causing silent fallback to audio/wav and OpenAI 400 rejection; (2) the hardcoded OpenAI Responses allowlist (only image/* and application/pdf) rejects legitimate file types at the SDK layer even when the provider supports them, forcing developers to maintain local patches; (3) FilePart's data field assumes all string values are base64, making it impossible to use URL strings without brittle workarounds, while ToolResultOutput already has proper discriminated types.
aliases: m4a mp4 misdetected as wav audio
signals.review_reason: Three distinct but root-cause-related file media type issues. Issue 14721 causes OpenAI API 400 rejection for any m4a/mp4 from iOS/Android/ffmpeg sources — a main flow failure with silent fallback masking the problem. Issue 14747 makes legitimate file types (CSV, docx, etc.) unusable at the SDK layer, forcing local patches — a significant developer experience and capability blocker. Combined, these represent a multi-vector file input failure that blocks core use cases.

source_issues.title: experimental_transcribe mis-detects m4a/mp4 files and sends them to OpenAI as audio/wav
source_issues.evidence: m4a/mp4 files are silently mis-identified as audio/wav because 'ftyp' box header is at byte offset 4 (not 0). OpenAI returns HTTP 400. Reproduction repo provided with byte-level proof and API response showing wrong MIME.

source_issues.title: Allow overriding hardcoded file media type filtering
source_issues.evidence: SDK layer rejects file types beyond image/* and application/pdf for OpenAI Responses path, even when provider supports them. Developers are forced to maintain local SDK patches. Privacy-sensitive apps rely on inline stateless file inputs and cannot use provider-side storage.

source_issues.title: Consider aligning FilePart and how files are handled in ToolResultOutput
source_issues.evidence: FilePart's string data field is assumed to be base64. Cannot use URL strings without workarounds. ToolResultOutput already has proper discriminated types (file-data, file-url, file-id) creating inconsistency. Real constraint: #12995 where a string-based provider reference could not be supported due to this assumption.

signals.topic: OpenAI-compatible streaming tool calls fail when function.name arrives in a later SSE chunk
signals.summary: OpenAI-compatible streaming tool calls fail when a provider sends the first tool_calls delta with an id and function.arguments but without function.name, then sends function.name in a later delta. The parser validates function.name on the first partial delta and throws before accumulating the later chunk.
aliases: streaming tool call name in later chunk
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure for streaming tool calls: when providers split the function name across chunks (valid behavior per accumulation), the SDK throws and the entire tool call fails. This is a streaming pipeline breaker, not a minor edge case, as tool calls are a core AI agent primitive.

source_issues.title: OpenAI-compatible streaming tool calls fail when function.name arrives in a later chunk
source_issues.evidence: Parser validates function.name on first partial tool-call delta and throws before accumulating the later chunk. Chunks that are individually valid after accumulation are rejected prematurely. Closed with fix merged.

signals.topic: Amazon Bedrock: raw <reasoning> tags leaked into LLM text response for OpenAI models during multi-turn tool use
signals.summary: Since @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock@4.0.85, OpenAI models accessed via Bedrock (e.g. openai.gpt-oss-120b-1:0) leak raw <reasoning>...</reasoning> XML tags into the final text response during multi-turn conversations with tool use. Root cause: a PR in v4.0.85 added an else branch that replays unsigned reasoning blocks (OpenAI's extended thinking returns reasoningContent without a cryptographic signature), causing raw tags to appear in user-facing output.
aliases: reasoning tags in text response bedrock
bedrock openai model reasoning content leak
signals.review_reason: LLM text response corruption with raw XML tags leaking to end users is a significant quality and trust issue. It occurs in a specific but real production scenario (OpenAI models on Bedrock with extended thinking in multi-turn tool use). The issue is reproducible and has a traced root cause to a specific PR.

source_issues.title: bug(amazon-bedrock): <reasoning> tags leaked into text response for OpenAI models on Bedrock during multi-turn tool use
source_issues.evidence: OpenAI models with extended thinking on Bedrock return reasoningContent without a signature field. PR #13972 added an else branch that replays unsigned reasoning blocks, causing raw XML tags to appear in the text output. Anthropic models are not affected. Multi-turn tool use is the trigger condition.

signals.topic: Vertex AI: broken URL generated when using location 'global' (required for gemini-3.1-pro-preview) — causes ENOTFOUND
signals.summary: When using @ai-sdk/google-vertex with location: 'global' (required for gemini-3.1-pro-preview), the SDK constructs an invalid URL: https://global-aiplatform.googleapis.com/... which does not exist (ENOTFOUND). The correct global endpoint is https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/... without the region prefix.
signals.review_reason: A startup crash: every request to gemini-3.1-pro-preview on Vertex fails immediately with DNS resolution failure because the required location parameter ('global') produces an invalid host. This blocks the primary use case (newest Gemini model on Vertex) entirely.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/google-vertex: Broken URL generated when using location: 'global' (Required for gemini-3.1-pro-preview)
source_issues.evidence: SDK constructs https://global-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/... which does not exist (ENOTFOUND). gemini-3.1-pro-preview requires location: 'global' per Google Vertex AI requirements. Closed with fix.

signals.topic: AI SDK v6: tool().parameters not read — prepareToolsAndToolChoice uses inputSchema (undefined), silently ignoring all tool schemas
signals.summary: In AI SDK v6, tool() sets the schema on .parameters but prepareToolsAndToolChoice and doParseToolCall read .inputSchema which is undefined. This causes all tool schemas to fall through to an empty default {"properties":{},"additionalProperties":false}, silently ignoring parameter definitions. The fix is a one-line change: use tool2.inputSchema ?? tool2.parameters instead of just tool2.inputSchema.
signals.review_reason: Critical functionality break in v6: all tool schemas are silently ignored, meaning parameter types are not enforced, validation is bypassed, and incorrect tool inputs are not caught. This is not a subtle edge case — it affects every user of tool() with zod schemas in v6. The silent failure (no error, no warning) makes it particularly dangerous.

source_issues.title: AI SDK v6: tool().parameters not read by prepareToolsAndToolChoice (uses inputSchema which is undefined)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: tool() sets .parameters but prepareToolsAndToolChoice reads .inputSchema which is undefined. All tool schemas silently fall through to empty default, breaking parameter validation and type enforcement. One-line fix identified.

signals.topic: notFound() returns HTTP 200 instead of 404 when streaming (loading.tsx present)
signals.summary: When a dynamic route has a sibling loading.tsx, calling notFound() renders the correct UI but returns HTTP 200 instead of 404, breaking SEO and caching semantics.
signals.review_reason: P0: Main flow blocking — incorrect HTTP status codes break SEO, caching, and require workaround implementations. Multiple versions affected (16.2.3, 16.3.0-canary.2). Has valid reproduction steps with curl commands showing the exact status code issue. Count=2 confirmed across two issues.

source_issues.title: 16.2.3 / 16.3.0-canary.2: notFound() returns HTTP 200 when sibling loading.tsx is present (HTTPAccessFallbackBoundary swallows 404 status under streaming)
source_issues.evidence: The notFound() function renders the correct not-found.tsx content but returns HTTP 200 instead of 404. This breaks SEO (search engines see 200), caching behavior, and proper HTTP semantics. The issue is traced to app-render.js where the HTTPAccessFallbackBoundary swallows the 404 status. Users are forced to implement middleware/proxy-layer 404 shims that duplicate DB round-trips.

source_issues.title: 16.3.0-canary.2: notFound() returns HTTP 200 when dynamic route segment has sibling loading.tsx
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #93253, same symptom. Closed with invalid link label but represents the same user pain.

signals.topic: router.refresh() triggers eager refetch of all in-viewport <Link> prefetches causing ~200x ISR Write increase in production
signals.summary: In Next.js v16, router.refresh() eagerly refetches every in-viewport <Link> prefetch instead of lazily as in v15, leading to a ~200x peak increase in ISR Writes in production.
signals.review_reason: P0: Detailed production evidence shows 200x cost increase and clear experience degradation. The user provided exact metrics from their production environment showing ISR Writes increased 50x after upgrading to v16, which is billable cost loss and significant UX degradation for end users.

source_issues.title: `router.refresh()` eagerly refetches every in-viewport `<Link>` in v16 (was lazy in v15) — ~200x peak ISR Writes in production
source_issues.evidence: Production data from sanity.io shows ISR Writes went from 7.1M/day (v15) to 358.5M/day (v16), a 50x increase. Single-day peak reached 1.52B (~200x). This is both a clear cost increase (ISR Writes on Vercel are billable) and significant experience degradation (every Link in viewport is eagerly refetched instead of lazily). The issue affects both next start and Vercel deployment.

signals.topic: Turbopack dev server crashes or enters EMFILE loop on macOS due to excessive fs.watch targets
signals.summary: Turbopack watches ancestor directories (/Users, /Users/<user>) and all app subdirectories on macOS, causing EMFILE (too many open files) errors and a broken dev loop.
aliases: EMFILE too many open files turbopack macOS
signals.review_reason: P1: Clear main flow blocking for macOS users with Turbopack — EMFILE errors break the dev server entirely. Not P0 because count=1, though multiple closed duplicates are referenced. Affects the primary development workflow.

source_issues.title: Turbopack dev on macOS hits Watchpack fs.watch EMFILE on ancestor directories and app subtrees
source_issues.evidence: Turbopack dev causes EMFILE (too many open files) errors on macOS because it watches ancestor directories like /Users, /Users/<user>, and all app subdirectories. This results in a broken dev experience where the server enters a failure loop. Webpack with polling works but bypasses Turbopack. This is a main flow blocking issue for macOS users using Turbopack.

signals.topic: Turbopack: next/dynamic lazy chunks retain stale module graph after source edits causing HMR failures
signals.summary: After editing a module imported by a dynamically-loaded component, HMR fails to update in Turbopack — stale chunk hash unchanged, not fixed by hard refresh or clean rebuild.
signals.review_reason: P1: Main flow blocking for Turbopack dev — HMR doesn't work with dynamic imports. Clear user impact on dev workflow with complete minimal reproduction. The issue persists across all workarounds and only Webpack build works.

source_issues.title: next/dynamic lazy chunk uses stale module graph after source edits (Turbopack)
source_issues.evidence: After editing a module imported by a dynamically-loaded component, HMR fails to update — cards still show old format with stale chunk hash unchanged. This is not resolved by hard refresh, rm -rf .next, or node_modules reinstall. Only next build (Webpack) works. Also compounds with Zustand persisted stores causing hydration mismatches and corrupted DOM. This is a main flow failure for Turbopack dev workflow.

signals.topic: updateTag causes hard refresh leading to 404 in parallel route navigation flow
signals.summary: Calling updateTag in a specific parallel routes modal navigation sequence causes a hard refresh that results in a 404 error page.
signals.review_reason: P1: Main flow blocking in a specific but valid navigation pattern involving parallel routes and server actions. Results in a 404 error page, which is a clear user-facing failure in a supported feature combination.

source_issues.title: UpdateTag is causing hard refresh
source_issues.evidence: In a parallel routes modal navigation flow, calling updateTag causes a hard refresh which results in a 404 error page. The issue only occurs in specific navigation sequences (first modal -> detail page -> second modal -> updateTag), not when starting directly on the detail page. This is a main flow failure for users relying on parallel routes with server actions.

signals.topic: Graceful shutdown (Ctrl+C) broken on Windows — SIGINT not forwarded to tasks
signals.summary: When running `turbo start` on Windows (PowerShell/CMD) or with `script-shell=sh`, pressing Ctrl+C immediately kills all child tasks instead of letting them shut down gracefully. The graceful shutdown sequence (intercepting SIGINT, sending to tasks, waiting for them to exit) is completely broken, causing data loss or inconsistent state in persistent dev servers.
aliases: Ctrl+C kills tasks without graceful shutdown
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues confirm the same root cause: on Windows (PowerShell/CMD) and with script-shell=sh, SIGINT is not forwarded to child tasks. This completely breaks the graceful shutdown mechanism that users rely on for stopping persistent dev servers. The evidence is concrete: tasks are killed without executing cleanup handlers, and the difference between working (WSL/bash) and broken (Windows/sh) is clearly demonstrated with logs. This is a main-flow blocker for any Windows user running `turbo start` or `turbo dev`.

source_issues.title: `SIGINT` is not forwarded properly when `script-shell=sh`
source_issues.evidence: With script-shell=sh, SIGINT is never received by the Node.js script. The graceful shutdown sequence never fires; task exits with 'Done' instead of completing the shutdown handler. Reproduced in WSL and Windows.

source_issues.title: Graceful shutdown does not work on Windows (PowerShell / CMD)
source_issues.evidence: On Windows PowerShell, pressing Ctrl+C immediately terminates child processes. The graceful shutdown log lines appear after the process exits, meaning tasks are killed before they can handle shutdown. Confirmed against WSL behavior which works correctly.

signals.topic: `turbo affected` fails to resolve `main` branch in GitHub Actions, causing all tasks to run unnecessarily
signals.summary: In GitHub Actions CI, `turbo affected` cannot resolve the base branch 'main' because the checkout only has the ref, not the full branch history. This causes turbo to fall back to 'all files changed' mode, making all tasks run on every PR instead of only affected ones — defeating the purpose of the affected-graph and wasting CI time.
aliases: affected mode falls back to all-tasks-changed in CI
signals.review_reason: Two issues (one long-standing, one new) confirm that `turbo affected` cannot resolve the main branch in standard GitHub Actions checkouts. This is a core CI feature failure: instead of running only affected tasks, turbo falls back to 'all tasks changed', causing full monorepo rebuilds on every PR. This directly wastes CI compute time and defeats the primary value proposition of turbo's affected-graph feature. Affects real production monorepos (e.g., next-intl) in their official CI pipelines.

source_issues.title: `affected` failing to resolve main branch in GitHub action
source_issues.evidence: GitHub Actions workflow using `turbo query affected --tasks build` fails with 'Failed to resolve base ref main: unknown revision'. Turbo falls back to 'assuming all files changed', causing all packages to build on every PR. Same repo was confirmed working after manually creating main branch. Verified with full reproduction workflow.

source_issues.title: `--affected` failing to resolve `main` even on full checkout
source_issues.evidence: Real-world monorepo (amannn/next-intl, 600+ stars) experiencing the same issue in GitHub Actions. Logs show git error 'fatal: ambiguous argument main: unknown revision'. Closed as resolved but reopened/resurfaced per issue #12650. CI money and time wasted on every PR.

signals.topic: `turbo watch dev` incorrectly re-runs package dev tasks when app source files change
signals.summary: In watch mode, when a source file inside an application (which depends on packages) is modified, turbo incorrectly triggers the `dev` script of all dependent packages, even though the packages themselves haven't changed and the app's dev server handles file changes natively.
aliases: turbo watch triggers unintended package dev tasks
watch mode false positive on app changes
signals.review_reason: This is a clear bug in the watch mode dependency graph. When an app file changes, turbo should not re-run package dev tasks (packages are already rebuilt by the dev server's own HMR). The behavior causes unnecessary, slow rebuild cycles that significantly degrade the watch-mode development experience. Count=1 but review_reason provides strong user impact evidence: persistent false-positive rebuilds of all dependent packages on every file save, introduced by a specific PR and confirmed with a video reproduction.

source_issues.title: `turbo watch dev` runs package `dev` when app depending on it changes
source_issues.evidence: User has a monorepo where apps run persistent Vite dev servers and packages run build scripts as their 'dev' task. When editing a file inside an app, turbo re-runs all dependent packages' dev scripts despite packages not being modified. Pinpointed to PR #12516 in canary 2.9.2-canary.4. Reproduced with video evidence.

signals.topic: `turbo prune --docker` generates invalid Bun lockfile, breaking Docker multi-stage builds
signals.summary: When using `turbo prune --docker` with the Bun package manager, the generated pruned lockfile (`out/json/bun.lock`) is malformed in a way that causes `bun install --frozen-lockfile` to fail in the Docker build stage. This breaks the standard Docker multi-stage build workflow that monorepo users rely on for production deployments.
aliases: Docker build fails with frozen lockfile after turbo prune
signals.review_reason: This blocks a critical production use case: Docker-based deployments for Bun monorepos. The pruned lockfile is invalid for frozen-lockfile mode, causing the Docker build to fail. This is a deployment pipeline blocker with a complete reproduction (public repo + Dockerfile + Docker build log). While count=1, the user impact is severe (CI/CD pipeline failure) and the evidence is unambiguous — the exact Docker command that fails is shown with the error message.

source_issues.title: `turbo prune --docker` generates invalid Bun lockfile; `bun install --frozen-lockfile` fails in pruned Docker stage
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction with public repo and Docker build. Root bun.lock installs fine with --frozen-lockfile, but the pruned out/json/bun.lock generated by turbo prune --docker causes 'lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen' error. Docker build fails at the install stage. Related to prior issue #11171.

signals.topic: Turbo fails to parse pnpm 11 lockfiles with multi-document YAML (configDependencies), breaking workspace resolution and task execution
signals.summary: With pnpm 11 using the `configDependencies` feature, turbo cannot parse the generated multi-document YAML lockfile. This causes workspace resolution to fail and results in pnpmfile hook execution errors that crash tasks. Standard `pnpm -r` works fine, proving this is a turbo-specific parser bug.
aliases: workspace resolution fails with pnpm 11 configDependencies
signals.review_reason: Turbo's pnpm lockfile parser cannot handle pnpm 11's multi-document YAML format (introduced with configDependencies). This causes a cascade of failures: workspace resolution fails, pnpmfile hooks cannot be resolved, and tasks crash. The evidence clearly shows turbo is the breaking factor — the same commands work with plain `pnpm -r`. This blocks adoption of pnpm 11, a significant version upgrade, and affects monorepos using configDependencies features.

source_issues.title: Turbo cannot parse pnpm 11 lockfiles with multi-document YAML (configDependencies)
source_issues.evidence: pnpm 11 writes multi-document YAML lockfiles with a pnpmfileChecksum frontmatter section. Turbo's lockfile parser throws 'deserializing from YAML containing more than one document is not supported'. This causes 'Unable to resolve workspaces' and 'Error during pnpmfile execution: Cannot find module .pnpmfile.mjs'. Tasks fail. Verified that plain `pnpm -r run typecheck` works correctly without turbo.

source_issues.title: vercel env add truncates multiline values when piped via stdin
source_issues.evidence: CLI reports 'Added Environment Variable' success but silently truncates to first line. Full PEM key (~1700+ chars) reduced to ~29-52 chars. Firebase Admin SDK fails at runtime with 'Cannot read properties of null'. No warning at set-time.

signals.topic: vercel env add NAME preview 命令因 git_branch_required 报错失败，CLI hint 与实际行为不一致
signals.summary: vercel env add MY_VAR preview 无法按预期添加环境变量到所有 preview 分支，始终报 git_branch_required 错误。CLI 错误提示本身（hint.next）给出的命令示例与报错行为互相矛盾，导致用户无法通过 CLI 管理 preview 环境变量，必须回退到 REST API。
aliases: preview env var CLI broken hint mismatch
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：环境变量管理是 CLI 最基础的操作之一。用户按 CLI 文档（--help 示例）和错误提示操作均无法成功，提示与行为相互矛盾，强制要求用户提供 git branch 而 hint 说无需提供。阻断 CLI 核心功能，用户必须改用 REST API。

source_issues.title: vercel env add NAME preview (without git branch) fails with git_branch_required despite CLI hint suggesting it works
source_issues.evidence: CLI v50.32.5 and v52.0.0 both reject 'vercel env add MY_VAR preview --value <value> --yes' with git_branch_required. The error hint itself advertises that exact command shape should succeed. Teams must fall back to REST API for all preview env vars.

signals.topic: Node.js runtime 在每次冷启动时输出 url.parse() DEP0169 弃用警告到生产错误日志，无法从用户代码侧消除
signals.summary: @vercel/node 内部使用 url.parse() 在每次函数冷启动时触发 Node.js DEP0169 弃用警告，写入 level:error 日志。用户代码无法从侧屏蔽——唯一缓解手段 NODE_OPTIONS=--no-deprecation 会同时压制所有弃用警告。
aliases: DEP0169 production log pollution cold start
signals.review_reason: 生产日志污染（production log pollution）：每次冷启动在 level:error 写入弃用警告，污染所有用户函数的错误日志，干扰告警和分页系统。不影响功能但严重降低生产可观测性，且无法从用户侧规避。

source_issues.title: Production Node.js runtime emits DEP0169 url.parse() deprecation warning on every cold start
source_issues.evidence: DEP0169 fires on every cold start of every function at level:error. grep of user bundle confirms no direct url.parse() usage — source is @vercel/node runtime. Cannot be silenced from user code; only mitigation suppresses ALL deprecation warnings.

signals.topic: vercel build 在 pnpm monorepo 下因硬编码基础设施路径无法在 CI（GitHub Actions 等）环境工作
signals.summary: vercel build 在 pnpm monorepo 中硬编码 /pnpm9/node_modules/.bin 等路径，这些路径仅存在于 Vercel 服务器上，GitHub Actions 等外部 CI 环境不存在。导致 vercel build + vercel deploy --prebuilt 这一 Vercel 官方文档推荐的 CI 工作流完全不可用。
aliases: vercel build pnpm outside Vercel infrastructure broken
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Vercel 官方文档推荐的 CI 部署工作流（vercel build + vercel deploy --prebuilt）对 pnpm monorepo 完全失效，用户被迫放弃 CI 方式构建，被迫直接推送到 Vercel 服务器。相关已知 issue 包括 #11475、#11607，表明影响范围广。

source_issues.title: vercel build broken with pnpm monorepos outside Vercel infrastructure (hardcoded PATH)
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause as #11475 and #11607. npm/yarn return path: undefined (system PATH) but pnpm returns hardcoded /pnpm9/..., only pnpm gets infrastructure-specific override. vercel build + deploy --prebuilt (Vercel-documented CI workflow) completely broken for pnpm monorepos.

signals.topic: @vercel/oidc 以 CJS shim 发布导致 esbuild 无法正确内联，使 Vercel Gateway 在 ai-sdk 集成中不可用
signals.summary: @vercel/oidc 以 CommonJS shim 形式发布，esbuild 不会内联 require 语句，导致输出中保留 require 调用。使用 ai-sdk 嵌入 Vercel Gateway 时，@vercel/oidc 被引入，当前只能通过 stub 规避，使 Vercel Gateway 在这类环境中完全不可用。
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：@vercel/oidc 被 ai-sdk → Vercel Gateway 链路依赖，CJS shim 导致 esbuild 无法正确打包，使 Vercel Gateway 在使用 esbuild 的环境中完全不可用。当前唯一解法是 stub，无法正常使用。

source_issues.title: CJS shim for @vercel/oidc breaks compiling
source_issues.evidence: esbuild keeps require statements as-is in output instead of inlining. When ai-sdk embeds Vercel Gateway, @vercel/oidc is pulled in. Workaround of stubbing makes Vercel Gateway effectively unusable by default in this setup.

signals.topic: Zed auto-update "Restart to Update" triggers infinite hang loop on Windows, preventing version upgrade
signals.summary: Clicking the "Restart to Update" button on Windows triggers an infinite loop in the updater, producing continuous hang detection logs and causing the app to freeze completely. The update never completes.
aliases: Zed hangs on restart to update Windows
signals.review_reason: Core updater workflow is completely blocked. The 'Restart to Update' action causes an infinite hang loop confirmed by Zed's own hang detection. The upgrade mechanism is broken on Windows for affected users, meaning users cannot apply security or feature updates.

source_issues.title: Zed hangs/crashes after clicking Restart to Update button
source_issues.evidence: Clicking Restart to Update on Windows causes continuous 'hang detected' log entries every second. App freezes indefinitely. Update never completes. Hang trace file repeatedly appended. Multiple occurrences confirmed across two consecutive version upgrades.

signals.topic: Zed account sign-in fails with "Invalid padding" decrypt error on macOS, blocking authentication
signals.summary: After completing the GitHub OAuth flow, Zed immediately errors with "failed to decrypt access token: Invalid padding", making account sign-in unusable on macOS.
aliases: GitHub OAuth token decryption fails macOS
signals.review_reason: Account authentication is a core gate for cloud features, sync, and extensions. The entire OAuth sign-in flow is broken for macOS users due to a token decryption failure. Users are completely blocked from signing in.

source_issues.title: Zed account sign-in fails with "failed to decrypt access token" / "Invalid padding" on macOS
source_issues.evidence: OAuth flow completes in browser, redirect to 127.0.0.1 occurs, then Zed shows 'Error: failed to decrypt access token' with base64 decode failure and 'Invalid padding'. Error reproduces across multiple re-authentication attempts. All sign-in attempts fail.

signals.topic: gopls (Go language server) fails to start when using custom shell configuration in Zed
signals.summary: When Zed is configured with a custom shell (e.g., tmux-based session), the gopls language server fails to start with 'go binary not found' because Zed spawns gopls in a stripped-down shell environment that lacks the user's PATH modifications.
aliases: Go LSP broken custom shell PATH
gopls cannot find go binary Zed custom shell
signals.review_reason: Go developers who use custom shell configurations cannot use the gopls language server, which is essential for Go development in Zed. The core language intelligence (autocomplete, diagnostics, go-to-definition) is unavailable for Go files when using shell customization.

source_issues.title: gopls broken by custom shell
source_issues.evidence: User configured tmux-based shell in Zed settings. Opening a .go file causes gopls to fail with 'Could not install the Go language server gopls, because go was not found'. Error confirmed in Zed log: 'Failed to start language server gopls: Could not install the Go language server gopls, because go was not found.' Shell configuration that adds to PATH is not inherited by the LSP child process.

signals.topic: Agent "Start New Thread" button does nothing after configuring valid Anthropic API key
signals.summary: After entering a valid Anthropic API key in the agent configuration, clicking 'Start New Thread' produces no response. The agent panel becomes non-functional for starting new conversations.
aliases: Agent new thread button unresponsive after API key config
Claude Agent start new thread broken
signals.review_reason: The Agent feature (the flagship AI coding capability) is entirely non-functional for affected users. After successfully configuring authentication, the primary action to start a new conversation fails silently with no feedback. This blocks the core use case of the agent.

source_issues.title: Agent: clicking "Start New Thread" after configuring Anthropic API key, does nothing
source_issues.evidence: User configured Zed with a minimal sandboxed profile, configured a valid Anthropic API key, and clicked 'Start New Thread' in the agent panel. Nothing happened. No error shown, no thread started. Confirmed on Linux Wayland.

signals.topic: Devcontainer Dockerfile build silently skipped — wrong container image used without user awareness
signals.summary: When a .devcontainer/Dockerfile uses a private upstream base image, Zed silently skips the build step and runs the wrong image. The Dockerfile layers are never applied, causing containers to lack expected users, tools, and configuration.
aliases: devcontainer build silently fails Dockerfile layers not applied
Dockerfile build skipped wrong image used
signals.review_reason: Devcontainer workflow is a key remote development feature. The build silently failing means users are working in a container that is completely misconfigured without any indication. Tools, users, and configuration from the Dockerfile are missing, potentially leading to failed commands, wrong permissions, and hours of wasted debugging.

source_issues.title: Devcontainer build silently skipped: upstream FROM image tagged as features image, Dockerfile layers never applied
source_issues.evidence: Dockerfile with multi-stage build uses private upstream base image. Zed tries to pull a local-only features image and fails silently, then tags the upstream base as the features image. Container starts without Dockerfile layers applied. User cannot exec as the expected container user because the Dockerfile-created user does not exist. No error is shown to the user about the build being skipped.
